```md
# Cat Annihilation — correctness audit log

Real-bug hunts across the native C++ (separate from the web-parity campaign,
which is about matching the reference; this is about actual crashes/UB/logic
errors). Each entry: a multi-agent audit (per-subsystem finders → adversarial
refutation → only survivors fixed), then each confirmed bug root-caused,
runtime- or code-verified, fixed at the root, and pinned with a regression.

## 2026-07-17 — Round 1 (7 subsystems, 9 confirmed bugs, all fixed)

Workflow: `cat-correctness-audit` (7 finders + adversarial verify). 3 finders
(progression, movement-camera, hud-ui-state) were transiently classifier-
blocked and re-run in Round 2.

| # | Sev | Bug | Fix | Commit |
|---|-----|-----|-----|--------|
| 1 | HIGH | `restart()`/`quitToMenu()` never reset WaveSystem — `wavesStarted_` latched, so a restart kept the pre-death wave + stale InProgress state; the next update spuriously auto-completed it and dumped the player into wave N+1 (verified: die wave 1 → Try Again → wave 2 with 0 kills in ~6s). | New `WaveSystem::reset()` clears the latch + all per-run state, called from both restart paths. Pinned in the gate menu-flow (`key:r` → expect fresh wave 1). | a4f322f |
| 2 | HIGH | `ExtractNodes` wrote `nodes[childIdx].parentIndex` with an unchecked asset-controlled child index — OOB heap write on a corrupt glTF. | Bounds-check + throw like the sibling guards. Hermetic-GLB regression (child index 5 on 4 nodes → throws). | 988a279 |
| 3 | MED | `ExtractBufferData`/`Joints`/`Weights` memcpy'd with no accessor-extent check — OOB read on a corrupt accessor. | All three take the buffer by ref + validate extent before memcpy. Hermetic-GLB regression. | 188d9a5 |
| 4 | MED | Melee/projectile weapon XP inflated 2-3× per swing: the 2-3-frame tolerance window re-ran the swing block against the same (now i-framed) dog, and the XP-awarding callback fired ungated. | `applyDamage` returns damage-landed; combo-commit + enriched callback gated on it. Replay regression (1 award/swing vs 3× pre-fix). | b083bf2 |
| 5 | MED | `--input-script` used raw `std::stof` → uncaught throw aborted the process on a malformed token. | `parseInputScriptFloat` (strtof, whole-token) skips + logs the bad command. | 9b8a903 |
| 6 | LOW | `enemiesForWave` computed `3 + wave*2` in 32-bit int → signed overflow (UB) for a fuzzed huge `--starting-wave`. | int64 + clamp to INT_MAX. Pinned. | 9b8a903 |
| 7 | LOW | `getScrollDelta()` always returned 0: the reset in `update()` (which runs after `pollEvents` populates it) zeroed the delta before the game read it. | New `clearScrollDelta()` called at frame top before `pollEvents`. (Latent — no consumer today.) | 98d4901 |
| 8 | MED | Enemy health bars projected with the camera's yaw/pitch (~2.6° off the scene's `lookAt`) + no shake → floated detached above the dogs. | `setEnemyBarCamera` takes the scene's exact eye/target; view = `lookAt(...)`. The projection-fix let the anchor revert to the web's cited 1.5. Before/after captures. | 71c16e0 |
| 9 | LOW | `enemiesForWave` overflow (folded into #6). | — | 9b8a903 |

All fixes: gate 4/4 green + unit suite green at each commit; every bug pinned
with a regression that fails if reverted.

## 2026-07-17 — Round 2 (the 3 re-run subsystems: progression, movement-camera, hud-ui-state)

Workflow `cat-audit-round2` (finders + adversarial refutation). 3 bugs
survived verification; each was runtime- or code-verified against the web
reference (the behavioral contract), fixed at the root, and pinned with a
regression that fails first if reverted.

| # | Sev | Bug | Fix | Commit |
|---|-----|-----|-----|--------|
| 1 | HIGH | Follow-camera mirrored to the FRONT of travel after any turn. The offset was `yawRot.rotate(cameraOffset_)` = `(+sinθ·d, h, cosθ·d)` — X wrong-handed vs the movement facing `(sinθ,0,−cosθ)`. At the spawn heading (θ=0, sinθ=0) it agreed with the correct offset, so every straight-walk check passed; after an A/D turn the camera flipped in front and W drove the cat toward the lens (verified: turn-left+walk → cat x=−12.1, camera x=−22.6, ahead of travel). | Compute the offset directly from the facing: `(−sinθ·cameraOffset_.z, cameraOffset_.y, cosθ·cameraOffset_.z)` → camera behind travel (post-fix cameraX=−1.7 ≈ playerX+10.4). Gate `menu-flow` now TURNS before asserting camera position (the prior straight-walk-only coverage was blind to the mirror). | a5cb947 |
| 2 | MED | Nine Lives revive never re-armed on restart. The leveling system survives a restart (level/XP/abilities carry over, matching the web's localStorage-restored reload), but the per-run `nineLivesUsed` latch was never cleared — a player who spent their revive last run began the next run unable to revive. The web's restart is `window.location.reload()` → fresh store with `nineLivesUsed=false`, so the revive IS available again. | `restart()` + `quitToMenu()` call `levelingSystem_->resetRevive()` (the run-scoped-reset invariant `WaveSystem::reset()` already upholds). Harness gained a `spendrevive` input-script verb + `reviveArmed` query; new gate stage `nine-lives-rearm` drives spend→GameOver→restart→re-armed. Fail-first proven (exit 4 with the fix disabled). | 609925f |
| 3 | LOW | Phantom hover SFX under web parity. The pause modal is ImGui-owned under `kEnabled`, and `render()`/`handleInput()` short-circuit — but `update()` still ran `updateButtons()`, whose per-frame hover hit-test against the stale legacy `m_buttons` rects fired `playMenuHover()` when the cursor crossed a now-invisible button. | Guard `update()` with the same `if constexpr (WebParity::kEnabled) return;`. Class-detector `scripts/lint-pause-parity-guards.ts` (`--selftest`, wired as gate stage 0) enumerates the "legacy PauseMenu path runs under parity" class across all three entry points; revert-refail proven. | bc8747e |

All fixes: gate green (now 7 stages: 2 lints + compile + build + cat-verify +
menu-flow + nine-lives-rearm) + unit suite (7,724,713 assertions / 1233 cases)
green at each commit.

### Harness investments made this round (per the owner's "give yourself more feedback" directive)

- `expect:` query **`reviveArmed`** — exposes `LevelingSystem::canRevive()` so revive lifecycle is scriptable.
- input-script verb **`spendrevive`** — injects "Nine Lives earned, revive spent" (reaching level 15 headlessly is impractical).
- `expect:` query **`cameraX/Y/Z`** (from Round 1) proved decisive here — the camera mirror was invisible to screenshots but a one-line assertion at a turned heading caught it.
- new class-detector lint **`lint-pause-parity-guards.ts`** — the first source-structural gate for the web-parity guard class.

### Investigated, NOT a bug (so it isn't re-dug — R16 proof-of-work)

**Player model facing after a turn (verifier's camera-fix follow-up).** Hypothesis:
the player mesh's `Quaternion(Y, yaw)` (PlayerControlSystem `processMovementInput`)
uses a different handedness than the movement facing `(sinθ,0,−cosθ)`, so the cat
would "moonwalk" (face the mirror of travel) after an A/D turn. **Verdict: not a
visible bug.** Evidence: (1) an engine-math probe (`Quaternion::rotate` +
`lookRotation`, the real headers) shows `Quaternion(Y,yaw)` only coincides with
the engine's `lookRotation(facing)` at yaw=0 — a genuine ABSTRACT inconsistency;
(2) BUT `lookRotation`/`lookAt` (which every enemy uses to face the player, and
they visibly do) is the tool for matching an EXTERNAL direction, whereas the
player's mesh yaw, the follow-camera offset (`cameraYaw_` hard-snaps to the mesh
yaw), and the travel facing ALL derive from the one `cameraYaw_` — they are
yaw-locked by construction, so a mesh-vs-travel mirror is structurally
unobservable through the follow camera; (3) rendered frames at spawn and after a
90° left turn + walk both show the cat's BACK to the camera (`.facing_shots/`,
regenerable). The inconsistency is harmless for the self-referential player rig;
it would only matter if the player mesh had to face an external target, which it
never does. No code change. If future work adds an external-facing player
orientation (e.g. lock-on), reuse `lookRotation`, not `Quaternion(Y,yaw)`.

```

`docs/parity/01-forest-environment.md`:

```md
# 01 — ForestEnvironment port spec

**Status**: spec written, no native code touched yet.
**User directive 2026-04-26**: only the survival/zombie-rounds experience
is in scope right now. `SimpleTerrain.tsx` was deleted as orphan code
(zero imports). `SimpleTerrainSystem.tsx` is the story-mode terrain and
is deferred until after survival is at parity.
**Web reference**: [src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx](../../src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx) (the 498-line component the survival scene actually mounts) + the surrounding `<SurvivalScene>` shell in [src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:165-211](../../src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx).

## Why this spec exists, and how I almost got it wrong

I initially wrote a spec for `SimpleTerrainSystem.tsx` (story-mode
terrain with cross-rivers, biomes, animated water, 5 bridges) thinking
it was the "full" version of `SimpleTerrain.tsx`. It is not. They're
for different scenes:

- `gameMode === 'survival'` → `<SurvivalScene>` mounts `<ForestEnvironment>`.
  No biomes, no rivers, no bridges. A flat grass plane with scattered
  pine/oak trees, bushes, and rocks. This is the zombie/wave mode.
- `storyModeActive === true` → `<StoryScene>` mounts `<SimpleTerrainSystem>`.
  Biomes + rivers + bridges + animated water. This is the storyline mode.

`SimpleTerrain.tsx` was an orphan — defined and exported but no import
in the active codebase. Removed in this iteration.

The native engine's `--autoplay` runs wave-survival, which maps to
`<ForestEnvironment>`, not `<SimpleTerrainSystem>`. So this spec
targets ForestEnvironment.

(Logged in `cat_port_session` as `kind='decision'` so the autonomous
loop, when it resumes, sees that file naming was misleading and the
user's directive is the source of truth on which path is live.)

## What ForestEnvironment + SurvivalScene render

### Scene shell — `<SurvivalScene>` in BasicScene.tsx (lines 181-211)

- Background clear color: `#87CEEB` (sky blue).
- Camera: perspective, position `(0, 12, 15)`, fov 75°, follows the
  player (CameraFollow updates lookAt every frame).
- Ambient light intensity 0.5.
- Directional light at `(10, 10, 5)` intensity 1, casts shadows.
- Fog declared as `['#87CEEB', 30, 150]` — but ForestEnvironment
  declares its own fog `['#4c6156', 30, 150]` and the LATER fog wins
  in three.js. **Effective fog while ForestEnvironment is mounted
  is dim forest green-grey `#4c6156`, near 30, far 150.**

### ForestEnvironment composition

#### Ground (`<ForestGround>` line 231-314)
- `<planeGeometry args={[10000, 10000]}>` rotated -π/2 on X, position `(0, -0.1, 0)`.
- Material: `MeshStandardMaterial` color base `#7fb069`, roughness 0.9, metalness 0, with a procedural canvas texture.
- Texture (256×256 canvas, `RepeatWrapping`, repeat 20×20):
  - Base fill `#7fb069`.
  - 300 grass-blade scribbles: `fillRect(x, y, 1, 2..6)` at random positions, color `rgb(127±10, 176±10, 105)`.
  - 15 dark spots: filled circle radius 1..4, color `rgba(45, 80, 50, 0.5)`.

#### Trees (lines 122-189 + placement logic 360-418)
Two placement passes:
1. **Random ring**: 100 trees, `angle = rand·2π`, `distance = 20 + rand·200`. Tree type = 70% pine (`>0.3`), 30% oak. Scale 0.5..1.0.
2. **Grid**: `for x in -300..300 step 80, z in -300..300 step 80`, skip if `sqrt(x²+z²) < 50`. Offset by `(rand-0.5)·40` to avoid grid look. 60% pine, 40% oak. Scale 0.4..1.0.

Each tree:
- Pine: trunk cylinder `r=0.3..0.4 h=4 sides=8` `#654321` rough 0.9, foliage sphere `r=2 segs=12` `#228B22` rough 0.8, both at trunk-y=2 / foliage-y=5.
- Oak: same trunk, foliage sphere `r=2.5` (wider canopy), same colors.
- Wind sway: `useFrame((_, delta) => { rotation.x = sin(t+offset)·0.01; rotation.z = cos((t+offset)·0.7)·0.01 }`, random initial phase per tree.
- Cast shadow + receive shadow on trunk; cast shadow on foliage.

#### Bushes (lines 194-206 + placement 421-435)
60 bushes in a `10..160` unit ring around origin. Sphere `r=0.7 segs=8`, color `#3a5f38`, roughness 0.9, scale 0.5..1.0, cast shadow.

#### Rocks (lines 211-226 + placement 442-456)
40 rocks in a `5..125` unit ring. Dodecahedron `r=0.5 detail=0`, color `#777777`, roughness 1.0, random Y rotation, scale 0.5..1.5, cast + receive shadow.

#### Fog
`<fog attach="fog" args={['#4c6156', 30, 150]} />` — declared inside ForestEnvironment so it overrides the SurvivalScene's sky-blue fog while ForestEnvironment is mounted.

## What the native engine has right now

The screenshot the user objected to (`C:/tmp/state/cat-verify-1777218893894.ppm`):
- Sky pale grey-blue.
- Uniform green plane (the existing CUDA Perlin heightmap rendered with no biome / texture variation, just a flat lighting term).
- Static tabby cat (player), two specks (NPCs), HP/WAVE HUD.

The native engine has:
- `Terrain` class at [game/world/Terrain.hpp](../../game/world/Terrain.hpp) — CUDA Perlin heightmap, vertex format with splat weights (grass/dirt/rock channels). Currently uploaded to ScenePass and rendered with `shaders/scene/scene.vert` + `scene.frag`.
- `Forest` class at [game/world/Forest.hpp](../../game/world/Forest.hpp) — places trees on the heightmap.
- `Environment` class with `groundColor` constant — looks unused for actual rendering since the scene is going through Terrain.
- No fog uniform plumbing visible in the terrain shader (need to verify in Step 2).

## Mismatch: native heightmap vs web flat-plane

The web port uses a flat 10000×10000 plane with a 256² grass texture
tiled 20×20 (so each tile is ~500 world units across). The native
engine generates a Perlin heightmap with 50-unit max amplitude.

**Two paths I could take**:

**Path A — keep the Perlin heightmap, dress it up.**
Tiles a 256² grass texture across the heightmap (UV = position.xz / tileSize), adds the wind-swept tree population around it, cone+sphere trees, dodecahedron rocks, sphere bushes. The native gets the *better* terrain (heightmap, not flat) but with the *same dressing* as the web port. Risk: if the user sees the heightmap and says "but the web port is flat, this is different", we revert. Reward: visibly more interesting world without losing the existing CUDA Perlin work.

**Path B — flatten the heightmap to match.**
Set `Params.heightScale = 0.0f` so the existing `Terrain` produces a flat plane, swap its splat-shader for a tiled grass texture, scatter Forest trees + add bushes/rocks. Strictly mirrors the web port. Risk: throws away the Perlin terrain investment unless we can re-enable it later via a config flag.

**Recommendation: Path A**, but parameterized so we can flip to Path B if it doesn't read right. The Perlin amplitude is just a `Params` field — set it to 0 if the user wants strict parity. Keep the heightmap for natural rolling ground that fog will hide most of anyway.

## Port plan (in order; each step ships standalone)

### Step 1 — procedural grass texture on the ground (highest visual delta)

- Generate a 256×256 RGBA8 texture in C++ matching the web port's canvas:
  - Base fill `#7fb069`
  - 300 randomized "grass blade" rectangles in `rgb(127±10, 176±10, 105)`
  - 15 dark spots in `rgba(45, 80, 50, 128)` (alpha=0.5 mapped to 128/255)
- Upload via existing VulkanTexture path.
- Bind to the terrain shader, sample with UV = `position.xz / 500.0` (10000 / 20 tiles = 500 world units per tile).
- Replace the `splatWeights`-based color with `texture(grassSampler, vUv)` until splat textures become a real feature.

### Step 2 — fog uniform plumbed into terrain + entity shaders

- Add a fog UBO or push-constant: `vec3 color, float near, float far`.
- Default: `(0x4c, 0x61, 0x56)/255 = (0.298, 0.380, 0.337)`, near=30, far=150.
- Sample `linearFog = clamp((dist - near) / (far - near), 0, 1)`, blend with output color.
- Apply in both `scene.frag` (terrain) and the entity fragment shader so the dog/cat/NPC distance fade matches the ground.

### Step 3 — bush + rock entities

- New `Bush` and `Rock` static-entity types: sphere-mesh and dodecahedron-mesh primitives, generated procedurally on engine startup (no GLB load needed for these).
- 60 bushes in `[10, 160]` ring + 40 rocks in `[5, 125]` ring around origin. Random scale, rotation. Cast shadow.
- Reuse the existing entity-draw path (the same one player + dogs go through).

### Step 4 — Forest population matches web port

- Audit the existing native `Forest` class: how many trees, where, with what variation.
- Adjust to match web port: 100 random ring trees + grid trees with center cutout + 30/70 oak/pine variation per pass. Scale ranges, foliage color `#228B22`, trunk `#654321`.
- Wind sway via per-instance phase (an animation hook in the entity update — small sin/cos applied to model matrix rotation).

### Step 5 — sky color + camera framing parity

- Background clear color: `#87CEEB` (currently is some other shade).
- Camera position `(0, 12, 15)` looking at player; FOV 75.
- Ambient 0.5 + directional from `(10, 10, 5)` intensity 1 (the engine probably already has these — verify).

### Out of scope for this spec

- Story mode / rivers / bridges / biomes — separate doc when survival has parity.
- Audio (`forest-ambient.mp3`) — the web port has it commented out; defer.
- LOD / instancing optimization — only after the visible parity lands.
- Replacing the Perlin heightmap with a literal flat plane (Path B) — only if Path A doesn't read right after Step 1+2 land.

## Acceptance check

Side-by-side PNGs in this directory:
- `01-forest-web.png` — captured from `bun run dev` in cat-annihilation, survival mode, screenshot.
- `01-forest-native-before.png` — current native (`C:/tmp/state/latest-pass.png` already captured).
- `01-forest-native-after-step-N.png` — one per step.

Pass criteria, evaluated by the user (not by a metric):
- Step 1: ground reads as grass with subtle blade variation, not a uniform green slab.
- Step 2: distant trees fade into forest green, not pop in/out at the camera frustum edge.
- Step 3: bushes and rocks visible scattered around the player.
- Step 4: tree population density + variety matches the web port within ±15%.
- Step 5: sky color matches; cat is centered in frame; first-person camera doesn't clip into ground.

## Anti-pattern guards (per session SESSION-NOTES.md)

- AP-IGNORE-WEB-SOURCE: every step traces to a specific file:line in
  `src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx` or `BasicScene.tsx`.
  Cited inline above. If a step has no citation, it's not in scope.
- AP-OPTIMIZE-BEFORE-PARITY: no instancing, no LOD, no GPU-side tree
  generation until Step 5 lands and the user signs off on visual.
- AP-TEST-INSTEAD-OF-PORT: no Catch2 cases for the procedural grass
  texture buffer-fill. Visual diff is the regression net.

## Status log

- `2026-04-26 ~16:40 UTC` — initial spec written for SimpleTerrainSystem (wrong target).
- `2026-04-26 ~17:00 UTC` — corrected by user; orphan SimpleTerrain.tsx removed; spec re-targeted to ForestEnvironment.tsx (the actual survival code path). Step 1 ready to start.
```

### Deliberate divergences (documented, not bugs)

- **Dog variant GLBs stay** as pure VISUAL variety (regular/fast/big rotation) with identical web stats — the owner's Meshy art direction; the web's single brown-box dog is the stats reference, not the art reference. Boss waves OFF under parity (`WebParity::kEnabled`), reachable with parity off.
- **Terrain stays 512×512** (web: 10000×10000 plane). With fog fully saturating by 150 units the edge sits deep inside pure fog color and reads as the same horizon; growing the extent would explode the Poisson forest generation.
- **Native-only survival flavor behind `WebParity::kEnabled == false`**: 20-spell elemental magic depth, per-variant stats, boss waves, finite 5-wave Victory campaign, free mouse-orbit camera.
- **Camera feel under parity**: yaw follows the cat's facing at 8 rad/s (~125 ms half-life) instead of the web's instantaneous snap (the snap reads as jarring at native frame rates), and a speed-scaled few-cm camera bob remains (sells locomotion on the glassy native framing). Position is hard-snapped exactly like web; geometry (10.5 back / 8.4 up) is exact.

## P1 gaps (gameplay-breaking, fix first) — ⚠️ SUPERSEDED by the 2026-07-17 sweep section at the top; retained as audit history. Do NOT work from these rows.

### [waves] Enemies-per-wave count formula — 🟡 partial
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:529-531): getEnemiesForWave(wave) = Math.floor((3 + (wave*2)) * 1.5). NOTE it uses wave*2, not (wave-1)*2. Wave1=7, Wave2=10, Wave3=13, Wave4=16, Wave5=19 — a strictly increasing linear ramp. (GAME_CONFIG.WAVES BASE_ENEMIES:3/ENEMIES_PER_WAVE:2/ENEMY_MULTIPLIER:1.5 exist at gameConfig.ts:67-75 but are NOT imported — LocalEnemySystem hardcodes the literals.) Same formula duplicated in WaveDisplay.tsx:77 for the 'N dogs this round' text.
- **Native** (game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:408-421 + game/systems/WaveDifficulty.hpp:86-128 + game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:203-210)
- **Gap**: Native uses a completely different formula AND much lower counts. Live config override (CatAnnihilation.cpp:204-205) sets baseEnemyCount=3, enemyCountMultiplier=2.0, then WaveDifficulty::calculateEnemyCount applies a dense/sparse sine overlay: floor(3 + (N-1)*2 + 2*sin(2*pi*N/3)), min 1. Wave1=4, Wave2=3, Wave3=7, Wave4=10, Wave5=9. Two divergences: (1) counts are far lower than web (4 vs 7 at wave 1); (2) the sine overlay makes counts NON-monotonic — wave 2 (3 dogs) spawns FEWER than wave 1 (4 dogs), which web never does. To match web this must be floor((3 + wave*2)*1.5) with amplitude 0.

### [waves] Win condition (endless vs wave-5 cap) — 🟡 partial
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:701,744): ENDLESS. On wave completion nextWave = currentWave + 1 with NO upper bound and NO victory/win state anywhere. The survival mode runs infinitely until the player dies. There is no 'you win' screen.
- **Native** (game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:427-433)
- **Gap**: Native ENDS the run: the onWaveComplete callback sets GameState::Victory once waveNumber >= 5 (CatAnnihilation.cpp:430-431), showing the Victory end-screen. So native survival stops at wave 5 while web continues indefinitely — a player who reaches wave 6+ on web has no counterpart on native. To reach 1:1 the wave-5 Victory cap must be removed (or web must gain a cap).

### [camera] Camera control model: locked-behind (player-driven) vs free mouse orbit — ✅ parity (verified headlessly 2026-07-16)
- **Web** (src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159): CameraFollow rigidly welds the camera behind the cat every frame using the PLAYER's rotation: cameraX = x - sin(rotation)*distance, cameraZ = z - cos(rotation)*distance (distance 10.5), height fixed 8.4, then camera.lookAt(x,0,z). There is NO mouse camera control at all.
- **Native**: `PlayerControlSystem::init` enables follow-yaw + the (0, 8.4, 10.5) offset for ALL play under `WebParity::kEnabled` (not just --autoplay), position hard-snaps in locked-behind mode, and `processMouseLook` early-returns (mouselook retired). Headless proof via the harness camera queries: at spawn cameraY=8.400000 exactly, cameraZ=+10.63 (≈10.5 behind, small yaw-lag catch-up); after walking −Z the camera trailed to −4.66. Remaining feel deltas are the two deliberate divergences below (yaw lag ~125 ms, speed-scaled bob).

### [enemies-ai] Chase / aggro engagement (enemies close on player) — 🟡 partial
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:211): No aggro gating whatsoever — every enemy ALWAYS moves toward the player every frame while distance > ATTACK_RANGE (1.2). Enemies spawn at 8-15m and immediately swarm inward from the moment they appear. There is no 'idle/wait' state.
- **Native** (game/systems/EnemyAISystem.cpp:60-83)
- **Gap**: Native uses an Idle->Chasing state machine: updateIdleState only transitions to Chasing when distance <= aggroRange. But DogEntity::create OVERRIDES aggroRange to the per-type stat (DogEntity.cpp:361,391) = 15 (Dog/BigDog), 18 (FastDog), 25 (BossDog) — contradicting the EnemyComponent.hpp:38 default of 80 and its own comment ('generous so dogs always close regardless of spawn radius'). Meanwhile CatAnnihilation.cpp:208-209 spawns dogs at minSpawnDistance 25 to spawnRadius 40. So virtually every wave dog spawns 25-40m out with an aggro radius of 15-18m: it stays in AIState::Idle and never chases until the player walks within 15m of it. Web dogs relentlessly swarm from spawn; native dogs passively wait. In the survival arena this reads as broken enemies that ignore a stationary player.

### [hud-ui-menus] Victory screen — 🔵 native-only
- **Web** (src/components/ui/GameModeSelection.tsx:322-333): Web survival is explicitly ENDLESS ('Face unlimited waves', 'Endless wave-based combat') — there is NO victory condition and no victory screen. Waves increase indefinitely: count floor((3+wave*2)*1.5), HP 100+(wave-1)*20.
- **Native** (game/ui/GameUI.cpp:420-521)
- **Gap**: Native ends survival at wave 5 → Victory state, showing a golden 'VICTORY! / All waves completed!' screen with Final Score + Total Time + 'Press SPACE to continue' (CatAnnihilation.cpp:430-431 caps at wave 5). This victory screen — and the finite 5-wave survival it implies — is native-only and directly contradicts web's endless survival. The screen itself is a HUD/menu divergence; the underlying finite-vs-endless run belongs to the wave/gameflow domain.

### [player-movement] Movement control scheme (tank vs camera-relative) — ✅ parity (verified headlessly 2026-07-16)
- **Web** (src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:280-297): Tank controls: W adds x+=sin(rotation)*speed, z+=cos(rotation)*speed (forward relative to the cat's own facing); S subtracts (backward). A/D do NOT strafe — they rotate the cat. Movement is purely along the cat's current facing axis. No camera-relative strafing exists.
- **Native**: the WebParity branch of processMovementInput implements exactly this (A/D rotate at kPlayerTurnSpeed, W/S drive along facing, Shift = run). It was INERT until 2026-07-16 — the branch early-returned before velocity→position integration (see Fix log) — so the audit correctly observed no key movement. Verified via the headless harness: `hold:w,2` → z −11.8 (walk speed 6 ✓); `hold:a,0.37;hold:w,2` → x −11.6/z +0.8 (~90° pivot then facing-locked travel ✓). Pinned by the gate menu-flow stage's `expect:playerZ<=-4`.

### [player-movement] Player turn/rotation via A/D keys (TURN_SPEED 4.25 rad/s) — ✅ parity (verified headlessly 2026-07-16)
- **Web** (src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:280-285): A adds to rotation, D subtracts, at rotationSpeed = GAME_CONFIG.PLAYER.TURN_SPEED (4.25 rad/s, gameConfig.ts:11) * delta * spinSensitivity (default 1.0). Facing is driven ENTIRELY by A/D key-held turning; the camera follows the resulting rotation. On mobile the turn rate is cut to 30% (index.tsx:271).
- **Native**: WebParity::kPlayerTurnSpeed drives the A/D in-place pivot in processMovementInput's parity branch. Headless probe: 0.37 s of A ≈ 90° (4.25 rad/s ✓) then W moved −X as the new facing dictates. (Mobile 30% turn cut not ported — native has no mobile build.)

### [player-movement] No mouse-look camera (web camera is rotation-driven only) — ✅ parity (resolved 2026-07-16)
- **Web** (src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-160): The web game reads NO mouse movement for camera control; the camera is derived purely from the player's rotation.
- **Native**: `processMouseLook` early-returns while follow-yaw is on, and follow-yaw is on for ALL play under `WebParity::kEnabled` (PlayerControlSystem::init) — the free-orbit mouselook only exists with parity off (recorded under Deliberate divergences / native-only flavor).

### [player-movement] Camera locked behind player by facing (dist 10.5, height 8.4, hard snap) — ✅ parity (verified headlessly 2026-07-16)
- **Web** (src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:142-157): CameraFollow every frame: cameraX = x - sin(rotation)*10.5, cameraZ = z - cos(rotation)*10.5, cameraY = 8.4, then lookAt(x,0,z). Hard snap.
- **Native**: init sets cameraOffset (0, kCameraHeight 8.4, kCameraDistance 10.5); locked-behind mode hard-snaps POSITION (the lerp only runs in the parity-off free camera). Verified via harness camera queries (cameraY 8.400000 exact; distance ≈10.5 behind facing at spawn and after travel). Yaw follows at 8 rad/s (~125 ms half-life) instead of the web's instantaneous snap, and a speed-scaled few-cm bob remains — both recorded as deliberate divergences.

### [progression] Cat level-up grants +max HP and heals player — ❌ missing
- **Web** (src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:869): Each cat level adds +20 healthBonus (HEALTH_PER_LEVEL=20, gameConfig.ts:95). player.maxHealth = baseHealth(100) + healthBonus (gameStore.ts:906), and on a max-HP increase the player is healed by the delta (gameStore.ts:907-908). This is a FUNCTIONAL, core survival-scaling reward: at cat L10 the player has ~280 max HP.
- **Native** (game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:3357)
- **Gap**: The native onLevelUp handler DOES the right thing (healthComp->maxHealth += HEALTH_PER_LEVEL=10, then full heal — CatAnnihilation.cpp:3362-3363), but it NEVER FIRES: LevelUpEvent is only subscribed (CatAnnihilation.cpp:856) and is never published anywhere, and LevelingSystem::setLevelUpCallback is never wired. So the player's HealthComponent stays at DEFAULT_HEALTH=100 (CatEntity.hpp:69) for the entire run — max HP never scales with level. Also the intended per-level gain differs (native +10 vs web +20). This is the single biggest survival-progression gap: in web survivability grows with level, in native it is flat forever.

### [progression] Nine Lives ability (L15) — survive a lethal hit — ❌ missing
- **Web** (src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:677): Unlocked at cat level 15. In damagePlayer(), if a hit would kill and abilities.nineLives && !nineLivesUsed, the death is cancelled and the player revives at 30% max HP (NINE_LIVES_REVIVE_PERCENT=0.3, gameStore.ts:679). FUNCTIONAL. Caveat: resetNineLives() (gameStore.ts:925) is never called anywhere, so it is effectively once-per-GAME, not the intended once-per-wave.
- **Native** (game/systems/leveling_system.cpp:246)
- **Gap**: Native implements the full revive (canRevive/useRevive revive at 50% max HP, resetRevive per-battle — leveling_system.cpp:242-257) but NONE of it is wired into the death path. The player-death branch goes straight to setState(GameState::GameOver) with no canRevive() check (CatAnnihilation.cpp:373-375). So at L15+ a web player cheats death once; a native player just dies. Revive % also differs (web 30% vs native 50%).

### [combat-abilities] Weapon switching / hotbar — ❌ missing
- **Web** (src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:288): 9-slot hotbar seeded with water-spell(slot0), sword(1), bow(2), shield(3); number keys 1-7 set activeSlot (LocalProjectileSystem.tsx:294-298 → setActiveSlot). The active item determines the current weapon (sword/bow/shield/spell), and combat/casting branch on activeItem.id/type.
- **Native** (game/entities/CatEntity.cpp:129)
- **Gap**: Native player is hardcoded to WeaponType::Sword (CatEntity.cpp:129) with no hotbar, no inventory, and no key binding to switch weapons. CombatComponent::equipWeapon exists but is never called for the player at runtime, so bow/shield/spell are all unreachable by a human player.

### [combat-abilities] Bow ranged attack — ❌ missing
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalProjectileSystem.tsx:235): With bow active, spacebar/left-click spawns an arrow projectile 2 units in front, speed 25 (LocalProjectileSystem.tsx:235-248), rendered as cylinder shaft + cone tip. On enemy hit deals 30 damage and awards 10 bow XP (GlobalCollisionSystem.tsx:126-129). Config BOW BASE_DAMAGE 25 / PROJECTILE_SPEED 15 (gameConfig.ts:38-44) is overridden by these live values.
- **Native** (game/components/CombatComponent.hpp:132)
- **Gap**: Native has full ranged infra (CombatComponent Bow: range 15, speed 1.2, damage 30; CombatSystem::processProjectileAttacks + spawnProjectile) but the player can never equip Bow (stuck on Sword) and autoplay never uses it, so a human player can never fire arrows.

### [combat-abilities] Shield block — physical barrier & front attack negation — ❌ missing
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:231): When shield is in slot 4 (index 3) and selected, it is a physical barrier: enemies are blocked and pushed away from a shield center 1.2 units in front of the player, collision radius 0.9 (LocalEnemySystem.tsx:231-338), and enemy attacks from the front 90° arc are fully negated — damagePlayer is skipped (LocalEnemySystem.tsx:356-375).
- **Native** (game/systems/CombatSystem.cpp:154)
- **Gap**: Native has a BlockState system (70% damage reduction, 0.2s perfect-block=100% + parry stun 1.5s; combat_components.hpp:26-108) driven by right-mouse (PlayerControlSystem.cpp:320-333), but the player entity is never given a BlockComponent (CatEntity adds only Transform/Health/Movement/Combat/Mesh), so startBlock is a no-op and the player cannot block. No shield item or physical enemy-blocking barrier exists.

### [combat-abilities] Player elemental spell casting — 🟡 partial
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalProjectileSystem.tsx:192): With a spell active, spacebar/left-click casts a colored sphere projectile 2 units in front, speed 15 (LocalProjectileSystem.tsx:192-234). On hit deals flat 20 damage regardless of element or magic level and awards 10 element-magic XP/hit, +15 on kill (GlobalCollisionSystem.tsx:130-137). No mana cost and no cooldown — fully spammable. 4 elements: water/air/earth/fire.
- **Native** (game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:603)
- **Gap**: Native ElementalMagicSystem is far richer (20 spells across 4 elements, mana, per-spell cooldowns, AoE, DOT, elemental strength/weakness) but has NO human-input cast path — processAttackInput handles only melee/block. Only autoplay casts, round-robin water_bolt/wind_gust/rock_throw/fireball at level 1 every 2.5s (PlayerControlSystem.cpp:529-609). A human player cannot cast any spell. Projectile speed is 25 (web 15) and damage is per-spell (water_bolt 20, fireball 30) vs web's flat 20.

### [gameflow-states] Survival end/victory condition (endless vs wave-5 cap) — 🔵 native-only
- **Web** (src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx): Survival is ENDLESS. Waves increment indefinitely; the only terminal state is player death (isGameOver). There is no win/victory screen -- a survival run continues until the cat dies. gameStore has no victory flag.
- **Native** (game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:427-433)
- **Gap**: Native survival is NOT endless: WaveSystem::setOnWaveComplete transitions to GameState::Victory when waveNumber>=5 while Playing (CatAnnihilation.cpp:430-432), showing a Victory end-screen overlay. So the native survival run terminates in a win after 5 waves whereas the web run never wins -- a fundamental, immediately-noticed flow divergence for the priority survival mode. (Wave-count scaling itself belongs to the waves domain; this entry is about the terminal Victory STATE.)


## Full matrix by domain

### waves

- 🟡 **Enemies-per-wave count formula** [P1] — Native uses a completely different formula AND much lower counts. Live config override (CatAnnihilation.cpp:204-205) sets baseEnemyCount=3, enemyCountMultiplier=2.0, then WaveDifficulty::calculateEnemyCount applies a dense/sparse sine overlay: floor(3 + (N-1)*2 + 2*sin(2*pi*N/3)), min 1. Wave1=4, Wave2=3, Wave3=7, Wave4=10, Wave5=9. Two divergences: (1) counts are far lower than web (4 vs 7 at wave 1); (2) the sine overlay makes counts NON-monotonic — wave 2 (3 dogs) spawns FEWER than wave 1 (4 dogs), which web never does. To match web this must be floor((3 + wave*2)*1.5) with amplitude 0.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:529-531: getEnemiesForWave(wave) = Math.floor((3 + (wave*2)) * 1.5). NOTE it uses wave*2, not (wave-1)*2. Wave1=7, Wave2=10, Wave3=13, Wave4=16, Wave5=19 — a strictly increasing linear ramp. (GAME_CONFIG.WAVES BASE_ENEMIES:3/ENEMIES_PER_WAVE:2/ENEMY_MULTIPLIER:1.5 exist at gameConfig.ts:67-75 but are NOT imported — LocalEnemySystem hardcodes the literals.) Same formula duplicated in WaveDisplay.tsx:77 for the 'N dogs this round' text.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:408-421 + game/systems/WaveDifficulty.hpp:86-128 + game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:203-210
- 🟡 **Per-wave HP scaling** [P2] — Native HP model is fundamentally different: per-variant base HP (Dog=50, BigDog=100, FastDog=25, BossDog=300 per WaveSystem.cpp:313-319) multiplied by a curved healthScaling = 1.0 + (N-1)*0.1 + 0.15*cos(2*pi*N/3), min 0.5. So a wave-1 regular Dog = 50 * 0.925 = ~46 HP — less than HALF of web's flat 100. Additive +20/wave (web) vs multiplicative ~+10%/wave with a cosine wobble (native). No single 100+(wave-1)*20 path exists on native.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:552-554: Every enemy HP = baseHealth(100) + (currentWave-1)*20. Flat, single enemy type. Wave1=100, Wave2=120, Wave3=140, Wave4=160, Wave5=180. maxHealth set equal to health. (Matches GAME_CONFIG.ENEMY.BASE_HEALTH:100 / HEALTH_PER_WAVE:20.)  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:303-320,423-429 + game/systems/WaveDifficulty.hpp:136-144
- 🔵 **Single enemy type per wave (no variants)** [P2] — Native spawns FOUR variants via a deterministic round-robin keyed on enemiesSpawned_ % 5: slot0/3/4=Dog, slot1=FastDog(spd9,dmg7.5), slot2=BigDog(spd4.2,dmg15) (WaveSystem.cpp:271-286, stats in EnemyComponent.hpp:62-85). Web has no variant system at all, so a single wave on native shows visibly different dog silhouettes/speeds that web never produces. This is a native-side addition beyond the web reference.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:402-497: Every spawned enemy is ONE generic type: a brown box 'dog' built from primitives, color shifts by health % (#8B4513 > #654321 > #3E2723). No BigDog/FastDog/BossDog concept; all enemies share ENEMY_SPEED=1.5, ATTACK_DAMAGE=15, ATTACK_RANGE=1.2, ATTACK_COOLDOWN=1000ms.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:266-286
- 🔵 **Boss waves** [P2] — Native marks every 5th wave a boss wave: isBossWave(N) = (N % bossWaveInterval==0), bossWaveInterval default 5 (WaveSystem.hpp:31, not overridden). On a boss wave EVERY spawn is a BossDog (WaveSystem.cpp:268-269): base 300 HP, moveSpeed 5, attackDamage 25, attackRange 3, scoreValue 100 (EnemyComponent.hpp:78-84), 2.0x scale. So native wave 5 = 9 BossDogs (~397 HP each). Web has no equivalent.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:529-768: None. Web has no boss wave concept — wave progression is a uniform ramp of identical dogs with no special wave, no boss enemy, no boss stats.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:431-433,268-269
- 🟡 **Win condition (endless vs wave-5 cap)** [P1] — Native ENDS the run: the onWaveComplete callback sets GameState::Victory once waveNumber >= 5 (CatAnnihilation.cpp:430-431), showing the Victory end-screen. So native survival stops at wave 5 while web continues indefinitely — a player who reaches wave 6+ on web has no counterpart on native. To reach 1:1 the wave-5 Victory cap must be removed (or web must gain a cap).
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:701,744: ENDLESS. On wave completion nextWave = currentWave + 1 with NO upper bound and NO victory/win state anywhere. The survival mode runs infinitely until the player dies. There is no 'you win' screen.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:427-433
- 🟡 **Inter-wave transition timing / duration** [P2] — Native uses a single flat transitionDelay = 5.0s (CatAnnihilation.cpp:207; WaveSystem sits in WaveState::Transition until stateTimer_ >= transitionDelay, WaveSystem.cpp:141) with NO post-clear 2s gate and NO special first-wave handling. Roughly ~5s silent gap vs web's ~2s+4s(=6s) staged sequence with a first-wave 3s pre-check. Different total durations and no first-wave special case.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:676-768: After all enemies cleared: wait 2000ms (waveCompleteTime gate), then set transition, show popup, and advance to next wave after a 4000ms setTimeout. First wave is special: waits 3000ms after wave-start before even checking completion, then the 2000ms clear-gate, then 4000ms popup (LocalEnemySystem.tsx:678-726). Spawning of the next wave is blocked (allowNextWaveSpawn=false) until the popup finishes.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:207 + game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:139-143
- ❌ **Wave transition / completion popup UI** [P2] — Native has a fully-built WavePopup class (WavePopup.hpp/.cpp) with showWaveComplete(wave, kills, time, nextCount) + showWaveStart + countdown + stats/next-wave preview — but showWaveComplete/showWaveStart are NEVER CALLED anywhere (grep of game/ finds only the definitions). The WaveSystem onWaveComplete callback (CatAnnihilation.cpp:427-433) only logs + maybe sets Victory; it never triggers the popup. Additionally the WaveCompleteEvent subscriber (CatAnnihilation.cpp:871 -> onWaveComplete:3648, which would show a 'Wave X Complete!' HUD notification + XP) is dead because WaveCompleteEvent is never published. Net: native shows NO wave-complete/transition screen at runtime.
  - web src/components/ui/WaveTransition.tsx:9-91: Two overlapping UIs. (1) WaveTransition (mounted BasicScene.tsx:184, wired via waveState.onStateChange): staggered fade-in 'WAVE X COMPLETE!' (t=0), 'WAVE X+1 STARTING SOON...' (t=800ms), 'N ENEMIES INCOMING' (t=1600ms). (2) WaveDisplay transition overlay (WaveDisplay.tsx:66-81): 'ROUND X' + 'THE DOGS ARE COMING...'/'MORE DOGS INCOMING!' + 'floor((3+wave*2)*1.5) dogs this round', shown for 3000ms.  · native game/ui/WavePopup.cpp:239-271
- 🟡 **Enemy spawn stagger interval** [P2] — Native spawnDelay = 1.5s (CatAnnihilation.cpp:206); WaveSystem::updateSpawning spawns one enemy every 1.5s (WaveSystem.cpp:81-85). A 4-dog native wave 1 trickles in over ~6s vs web's ~1.4s. 7.5x slower spawn cadence dramatically changes early-wave pacing/pressure.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:568-595: All wave enemies are created up front, then revealed with a 200ms stagger: setTimeout(..., index * 200). A 7-dog wave 1 is fully on-field within ~1.4s. (GAME_CONFIG.WAVES.SPAWN_DELAY:200 matches, though not imported.)  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:206 + game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:77-91
- 🟡 **Spawn ring radius & angular distribution** [P2] — Native minSpawnDistance=25, spawnRadius=40 (CatAnnihilation.cpp:208-209) — enemies spawn 25-40m out vs web's 8-15m, so they take much longer to reach the player. Also native uses RANDOM angle AND random radius (uniform_real_distribution, WaveSystem.cpp:376-382) rather than web's evenly-spaced ring, so native can cluster spawns on one side instead of encircling. Native additionally snaps spawn Y to terrain height (WaveSystem.cpp:401-403); web is flat y=0.5.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:526-550: SPAWN_DISTANCE=15, MIN_SPAWN_DISTANCE=8. Enemies placed on a ring around the player at EVENLY-SPACED angles: angleStep = 2*pi/enemyCount, angle = i*angleStep, distance = 8 + random*(15-8). Deterministic even encirclement, y=0.5.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:208-209 + game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:376-405
- ✅ **Wave progression state machine** [P3] — Native has an explicit WaveState enum (Spawning/InProgress/Completed/Transition, WaveSystem.hpp:15-20) driven by update(dt) switch (WaveSystem.cpp:52-75). Conceptually equivalent lifecycle (spawn -> fight -> complete -> transition -> next). Completion detected by spawnedEnemies_ emptying, counting dead/dying dogs as cleared (WaveSystem.cpp:113-137). Different implementation but functionally parallel; the observable differences are captured in the count/timing/UI features above.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:655-770: Implicit state via refs: waveStarted, isWaveTransition, waveCompleteTime, allowNextWaveSpawn, isFirstWave. Flow: no-enemies+!started+allowed -> spawnWave; started+0 enemies -> completion timers -> transition -> setCurrentWave(next). Completion detected purely by localEnemies.length===0.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:52-144
- 🟡 **Permanent wave/round counter HUD** [P3] — Native HUD shows live wave number (setWave from waveSystem_->getCurrentWave(), CatAnnihilation.cpp:1383-1384) PLUS a 'remaining/total' enemy count web lacks. But the displayed TOTAL is computed with the LINEAR formula base + (wave-1)*mult = 3+(wave-1)*2 (CatAnnihilation.cpp:1386-1388), while the ACTUAL spawn count comes from the dense/sparse curve (calculateEnemyCount). So the native HUD 'total' is wrong for most waves (e.g. shows 5 for wave 2 but only 3 dogs actually spawn). Web's counter has no such mismatch because it has no total.
  - web src/components/ui/WaveDisplay.tsx:52-64: Always-on counter: 'ROUND {currentWave}' + 'SURVIVE THE HORDE', updated live via waveState subscription; animates on wave change. Shows only the round number (no enemy-remaining count).  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:1382-1391
- ✅ **Lose condition (game over on player death)** [P3] — Native transitions to GameState::GameOver on player death (HealthSystem death callback), with a GameOver overlay + restart/quit input (updateGameOver, CatAnnihilation.cpp:2069-2082). Equivalent lose semantics. (Native also has the extra Victory exit at wave 5 covered in the win-condition feature.)
  - web src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:722-795: Enemies call damagePlayer(15) on contact (LocalEnemySystem.tsx:372); when player health reaches 0 the store flips isGameOver and the GameOverScreen shows with stats + restart. This is the only failure/exit path in survival.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2069-2082
- 🟡 **Wave-complete XP bonus** [P3] — Native's onWaveComplete (CatAnnihilation.cpp:3648-3667) would award event.xpReward via levelingSystem_ on wave complete, but it fires off WaveCompleteEvent which is never published, so it is also dead. Both sides therefore lack a live wave-complete XP bonus — parity in effect, but both are non-functional rather than intentionally absent. Low impact.
  - web src/config/gameConfig.ts:80-81: GAME_CONFIG.EXPERIENCE.WAVE_BONUS_BASE:25 and WAVE_BONUS_PER_LEVEL:5 are DEFINED but never applied — grep shows no consumer. The only XP in survival is per-kill: addCatXP(5) and weapon kill XP 15 (LocalEnemySystem.tsx:637-651). So there is effectively NO wave-completion XP bonus at runtime (dead config).  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:3648-3667

> notes: SURVIVAL is the in-scope mode; all findings above are survival-mode. No story-mode-specific wave logic exists (waves are survival-only on both sides).

LIVE-PATH CONSTANT WARNING (critical for any numeric fix): On the WEB side, GAME_CONFIG.WAVES/ENEMY/EXPERIENCE constants in src/config/gameConfig.ts are NOT imported by LocalEnemySystem.tsx — it hardcodes floor((3+wave*2)*1.5), HP 100+(wave-1)*20, spd 1.5, dmg 15, spawn 8-15, 200ms stagger. Fix parity against the HARDCODED literals, not the config file. On the NATIVE side there are THREE competing wave configs and only ONE is live: (1) game/config/GameplayConfig.hpp::Waves (INITIAL_ENEMY_COUNT 5, ENEMY_COUNT_SCALING 1.3, BOSS_FREQUENCY 10, WAVE_BREAK_DURATION 15) — DEAD, unused; (2) game/config/BalanceConfig.hpp::Waves (ENEMY_COUNT_BASE 5, +3/wave, HEALTH_SCALING 1.08, ELITE_WAVE_FREQUENCY 5) — DEAD, unused; (3) the WaveConfig struct default (base 5, mult 1.5, bossInterval 5) OVERRIDDEN at runtime by CatAnnihilation.cpp:203-210 to base 3 / mult 2.0 / spawnDelay 1.5 / transitionDelay 5.0 / minSpawn 25 / spawnRadius 40, then passed through WaveDifficulty's sine/cosine curve — this override + WaveDifficulty.hpp is the ONLY executed path. Ignore GameplayConfig/BalanceConfig when reconciling numbers.

The native WaveSystem also exposes setInitialWave() / --starting-wave CLI flag (WaveSystem.hpp:111) for CI/portfolio boss captures — native-only tooling, no web equivalent, not a gameplay parity gap.

Highest-leverage fixes to reach 1:1 survival: (P1) match enemy-count formula to floor((3+wave*2)*1.5) by zeroing the WaveDifficulty countAmplitude and setting base/mult to the web ramp; (P1) remove the wave-5 Victory cap so native is endless like web; (P2) wire the WavePopup (it is fully built but never called) to reproduce web's wave-complete transition screen; (P2) reconcile HP to flat 100+(wave-1)*20 and spawn cadence/ring (200ms stagger, 8-15m even ring) — though note native's 4-variant + boss-wave design is a deliberate richer superset that web lacks, so a true 1:1 would require either downgrading native to one dog type or adding variants/bosses to web.

### audio

- 🟡 **Ambient environment loop (forest ambient / wind)** [P3] — Native playAmbientWind(volume=0.3f) mirrors the web's 0.3 loop volume: it creates a looping, relative-to-listener source on the Ambient channel (channel vol 0.5, GameAudio.cpp:27). BUT it is NEVER invoked anywhere in game/ (grep of game/ finds only the definition) so it is dead just like web, and it loads sfx/footstep.wav as the 'ambient_wind' buffer (GameAudio.cpp:361, a stated fallback 'until proper ambient is added') rather than a forest/wind ambient. Both sides: no ambient audio actually plays.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:342-358: The ONLY audio code in the entire web reference. useEffect creates new Audio('/assets/sounds/forest-ambient.mp3'), sets audio.loop=true and audio.volume=0.3, but audio.play() is COMMENTED OUT at line 350 ('// Uncomment when you have the sound file') and the referenced mp3 does not exist in public/ (public/ has only .svg files, and the folder is /assets/sounds not /assets/audio). Net: no ambient sound ever plays. DEAD code.  · native game/audio/GameAudio.cpp:274-291
- 🔵 **Background music system (menu / gameplay / victory / defeat) + cross-fade** [P3] — Native has a full music subsystem wired to game states: playMenuMusic = crossFadeMusic(menu_music.wav, 1.0s, looping, Music channel vol 0.7) on MainMenu (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2145 + GameUI.cpp:181); playGameplayMusic = crossFadeMusic(gameplay_music.wav, 1.5s, looping) on Playing (2169 + GameUI.cpp:186); playVictoryMusic = one-shot victory_sting.wav gain 1.0 on Victory (2216 + GameUI.cpp:203); playDefeatMusic = one-shot defeat_sting.wav gain 1.0 on GameOver (2202 + GameUI.cpp:199). All four WAVs exist under assets/audio/sfx/ but no gameplay code calls them — e.g. player death goes to GameOver -> defeat music instead of playPlayerDeath. Dead on both sides.
  - web src/ (no audio; web has no SFX): No sword-swing, projectile-fire, projectile-hit, or player-death sounds. Web has no SFX layer.  · native game/audio/GameAudio.cpp:214-240
