- 🔵 **3D positional/spatial audio (OpenAL distance model + doppler)** [P3] — Native routes positional SFX (playSound with a 3D position: enemy death/hit, projectile hit) through OpenAL with a distance model plus doppler (alDopplerFactor 1.0, alSpeedOfSound 343.3) and a listener; 2D sounds/music use setRelativeToListener(true). Web has no equivalent capability.
  - web src/ (no audio; no THREE.AudioListener / PositionalAudio): Web has no spatialized audio (and no audio at all) — no THREE.AudioListener, PositionalAudio, or Web Audio panning.  · native engine/audio/AudioEngine.cpp:70-79
- ✅ **Default-silent behavior (no audible output on a normal launch)** [P3] — OBSERVABLE parity: both sides emit NO sound on a default run. Mechanisms differ — native has a complete, fully-wired audio system, but AudioEngine::initialize() returns false unless the env var CAT_AUDIO is set to a non-'0' value (owner directive 2026-04-26, AudioEngine.cpp:20-42): the OpenAL device is never opened and playSound/playSound2D early-return, so all the native wiring produces silence. Web is silent simply because no audio was implemented. Launch native with CAT_AUDIO=1 to enable everything above.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:350: Web is silent by default: its only audio (the ambient loop) has audio.play() commented out and its source file is absent, so a normal run of the web game produces no sound whatsoever.  · native engine/audio/AudioEngine.cpp:37-42

> notes: DOMAIN INVERSION: This is the opposite of the usual parity direction. The WEB side (the designated reference/source-of-truth) has essentially NO audio — the only audio code in all of src/ is a dead, commented-out ambient forest loop at src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:342-358 (new Audio('/assets/sounds/forest-ambient.mp3'), loop=true, volume=0.3, but play() is commented out and the mp3 file does not exist; even the path folder /assets/sounds is wrong vs the actual /assets/audio). No music, no SFX, no UI/wave/level-up/combat sounds, no Howler/THREE.Audio/AudioContext anywhere in src/ or public/ (verified by grep; public/ contains only .svg). So for strict 1:1 parity with the web reference, the native game is NOT missing anything audio-wise — it EXCEEDS the reference, and its default silent state (via the CAT_AUDIO gate) actually matches the web's default silence.

ASSET LOCATION NUANCE: The 15 SFX WAVs (assets/audio/sfx/: sword_swing, sword_hit, projectile_fire, projectile_hit, enemy_hurt, enemy_death, player_hurt, player_death, footstep, jump, land, menu_click, menu_hover, pickup, wave_complete) and 4 music WAVs (assets/audio/music/: menu_music, gameplay_music, victory_sting, defeat_sting) belong to the NATIVE build only (mirrored into build-ninja/assets/audio/). They are NOT web-served (a Vite/web build serves from public/, which has none), so they do not give the web side any audio. Note jump.wav, land.wav, sword_hit.wav exist as assets but have NO play method in GameAudio at all (orphaned assets).

NATIVE-SIDE DEAD/BROKEN AUDIO (for a future parity/QA pass, not web gaps): playSwordSwing, playProjectileFire, playProjectileHit, playPlayerDeath, playError, and playAmbientWind are all defined in GameAudio but never invoked anywhere in game/. playSound2D(\"quest_complete\") at CatAnnihilation.cpp:3346 references a sound name that loadAllSounds never registers, so it no-ops even with audio enabled. Several loaded names use explicit fallbacks: WAVE_START->wave_complete.wav, LEVEL_UP->pickup.wav, ERROR->menu_click.wav, ENEMY_HIT->enemy_hurt.wav, AMBIENT_WIND->footstep.wav.

TOOLING: assets/audio/generate_audio.py (20KB) is a native-only Python generator that procedurally synthesizes the WAV assets; no web equivalent.

CONCLUSION FOR PARITY WORK: There are no P1/P2 audio parity gaps for the survival experience — the reference has no audio and the port's audio is silent by default. All entries are P3 polish. If the intent later flips to 'the native audio system IS the target and web should match', then everything above becomes a web-side implementation task instead — but per the stated method (web = reference), native is at/above parity here.

### camera

- 🟡 **Camera control model: locked-behind (player-driven) vs free mouse orbit** [P1] — In interactive human play (Start from menu, no --autoplay), the native camera is a FREE mouse-look orbit: processMouseLook writes cameraYaw_/cameraPitch_ from raw mouse delta (sensitivity 0.002) and the cat is steered by camera-relative WASD strafe while it rotates to face movement (PlayerControlSystem.cpp:162-182). The web-style locked-behind camera (setFollowPlayerYaw, which hard-snaps cameraYaw_ to the player's facing yaw — the true 1:1 equivalent of web CameraFollow) EXISTS but is enabled ONLY inside the --autoplay CLI branch (main.cpp:833); a normal launched game never enables it. So a human sees an entirely different control paradigm (orbit-with-mouse + WASD strafe) than the web reference (no mouse camera + tank-turn welded-behind view).
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159: CameraFollow rigidly welds the camera behind the cat every frame using the PLAYER's rotation: cameraX = x - sin(rotation)*distance, cameraZ = z - cos(rotation)*distance (distance 10.5), height fixed 8.4, then camera.lookAt(x,0,z). There is NO mouse camera control at all — the mouse only triggers attack/shield (CatCharacter/index.tsx:199-227). The camera direction is ALWAYS the cat's facing; the player turns the view by turning the cat with A/D (tank controls, CatCharacter/index.tsx:280-285).  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:242-278, game/main.cpp:825-836
- 🟡 **Perspective camera FOV** [P2] — Native hardcodes the projection FOV to 60 degrees (makeVulkanPerspective(60.0f * DEG_TO_RAD, aspect, 0.1f, 2000.0f)). Web uses 75. The 15-degree narrower native FOV produces a visibly tighter, more zoomed-in framing (less of the world visible around the cat). No FOV constant exists in any native config file — it is a literal in the render call.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:193: <PerspectiveCamera makeDefault position={[0,12,15]} fov={75} /> — vertical FOV 75 degrees (same value in StoryScene BasicScene.tsx:225 and the error-boundary fallback :67).  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:1574-1575
- 🟡 **Camera follow offset (distance behind + height above player)** [P2] — Live native cameraOffset_ = (0, 3.0, 6.0) => only 6 units back and 3 units up (rotated by yaw/pitch; setCameraOffset is never called anywhere in game/, so this default is authoritative). With lookAt at player+0.75 the native downward pitch in locked-behind mode is ~20.6 degrees (atan2(2.25,6)). Native camera is dramatically CLOSER (6 vs 10.5 back) and LOWER/shallower (3 vs 8.4 up, 20.6deg vs 38.7deg down) than web. The large header comment block (PlayerControlSystem.hpp:411-417) claiming the offset was 'matched to web port ... 12 up + 15 back' is stale/contradicted by the actual value on line 418, which is (0,3,6).
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:145-146: distance = 10.5 (horizontal distance behind player; comment '30% closer: 15 * 0.7'), height = 8.4 (fixed world-Y above ground; comment '30% closer: 12 * 0.7'). Camera sits 10.5 units behind and 8.4 up, looking at ground under the player => ~38.7 degrees downward pitch (atan2(8.4,10.5)). NOTE: GAME_CONFIG.PLAYER.CAMERA_DISTANCE=15 and CAMERA_HEIGHT=12 (gameConfig.ts:12-13) are DEAD constants — the live CameraFollow hardcodes 10.5/8.4 and never imports them.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.hpp:418
- 🟡 **LookAt target anchor (ground vs torso)** [P3] — Native aims at playerXform->position + (0, 0.75, 0) (cat torso), deliberately NOT y=0, because native terrain sits at y~=25 (not 0 like web) so a y=0 aim would point the camera far below the cat (comment CatAnnihilation.cpp:1516-1537). This is a deliberate adaptation to the native terrain height, but it means the framing anchor differs from web (torso-centered vs feet/ground-centered). Minor framing difference; native's choice is arguably more correct for its terrain.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:155: camera.lookAt(x, 0, z) — aims at the player's XZ at ground level y=0 (survival player.y is always 0). The cat's feet sit near the crosshair with the body filling upward.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:1538-1539
- 🔵 **Mouse-look camera control (yaw/pitch orbit + pitch clamp)** [P2] — Native adds a full free-look orbit: cameraYaw_ -= mouseDx*0.002, cameraPitch_ -= mouseDy*0.002, pitch clamped to [-1.4 rad (~-80deg), +0.5 rad (~+28deg)] (cameraMinPitch_/cameraMaxPitch_, PlayerControlSystem.hpp:459/466), yaw wrapped to [-PI,PI]. This is active in all human play. It is native-only relative to the web reference and is the mechanism behind the P1 control-model divergence.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:199-227: Web has ZERO mouse-driven camera control. Mouse buttons only perform sword attack (left/space) and shield bash (right); contextmenu is suppressed. The camera can never be orbited, pitched, or aimed with the mouse — view direction is 100% a function of the cat's A/D tank rotation.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:242-278
- 🟡 **Camera position smoothing (snap vs lerp)** [P3] — Native human/mouse mode LERPS the camera position toward the desired pose at cameraFollowSpeed_ * dt (10 * dt, ~0.16/frame at 60fps), so the camera trails the player smoothly instead of snapping. (Only the autoplay follow-yaw locked mode hard-snaps position, PlayerControlSystem.cpp:910, matching web.) Web = instant snap; native human = smoothed follow — a subtle but perceptible motion-feel difference.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:152-155: Camera position is set DIRECTLY every frame (camera.position.x/z/y = ...) with no interpolation — an instantaneous hard snap to the ideal behind-player pose each frame.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:911-917
- 🔵 **Camera-ground collision clamp** [P3] — Native clamps cameraPosition_.y to at least terrain height + 0.5m (sampled at the camera's XZ) so steep mouse-pitch cannot push the camera under the solid ground. This exists specifically because native added mouse pitch (which web lacks); it is native-only polish with no web counterpart.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159: Web camera has NO ground collision. Height is a fixed 8.4 and can never dip below the ground because there is no pitch control to push it down; nothing samples terrain for the camera.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:944-953
- 🔵 **Speed-synced camera bob** [P3] — Native adds a locomotion-synced camera bob: vertical bob freq 4-6 Hz (4.0 + 2.0*normSpeed), amplitude scales as normSpeed^2 up to 4cm vertical / 2cm lateral, lateral at half frequency for a figure-8 head trace, phase accumulator to avoid speed-change snaps. Native-only presentation enhancement absent from web.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159: Web camera has no bob/head-sway — the follow is mathematically glassy (direct position assignment only).  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:1001-1044
- 🔵 **Camera punch on melee attack** [P3] — Native fires a 0.25s cinematic camera punch on each melee attack start (detected via attackCooldown frame-to-frame jump > 0.05s): asymmetric triangle envelope peaking at 20% phase, 10cm back along camera-back + 4cm up. Native-only combat-feel polish absent from web.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159: Web camera does not react to attacks — no kick, punch, or recoil on sword/shield use.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:1096-1147
- 🔵 **Kill-feedback camera shake** [P3] — Native adds triggerCameraShake (hard-clamped <=0.25m peak, quadratically-decaying 3D noise) fired on enemy kills, scaled per dog tier, applied to camPos only (not camTarget so the cat stays centered). Native-only feedback polish absent from web.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159: Web camera has no shake on enemy kills or any other event.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:3175-3216, applied at 1557-1567
- 🔵 **Cinematic orbit camera** [P3] — Native adds a deterministic cinematic orbit that advances cameraYaw_ by yawRate*dt (default 0.5 rad/s, ~12.6s per revolution) around the player for portfolio captures, enabled via --cinematic-orbit-camera CLI flag (autoplay-context only). Native-only demo feature; not part of interactive play on either side.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-159: Web has no orbital/turntable camera mode of any kind.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:820-832, game/main.cpp:815-824
- ❌ **Menu / cat-preview camera** [P3] — Native MainMenu is an ImGui 2D panel (MainMenu.cpp) with no 3D cat-preview viewport or preview camera. The gameplay 3D scene only renders in GameState::Playing (CatAnnihilation.cpp:1457); in MainMenu there is no scene camera at all. Web's fov-50 [0,0,5] menu preview camera has no native equivalent. (Menu/customization cosmetic.)
  - web src/components/ui/GameModeSelection.tsx:186: The start screen renders a live 3D cat customization preview in its own R3F Canvas with camera={{ position: [0,0,5], fov: 50 }} — a dedicated front-facing preview camera separate from the gameplay camera.  · native game/ui/MainMenu.cpp
- 🟡 **Camera-sensitivity setting semantics** [P3] — Native 'sensitivity' means mouse-look rate: PlayerControlSystem uses a hardcoded mouseSensitivity_ = 0.002f. The MainMenu Settings slider writes gameConfig->controls.mouseSensitivity (and invertMouseY), but PlayerControlSystem never reads GameConfig (setMouseSensitivity is never called anywhere in game/), so the native sensitivity/invert-Y sliders appear orphaned/non-functional. Because web has no mouse-look and native's 'sensitivity' governs a control axis web doesn't have, the setting is semantically non-parallel and its native wiring is likely dead.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:98-101,272: Web 'sensitivity' (catSpinSensitivity, default GAME_CONFIG.INPUT.DEFAULT_SENSITIVITY=1.0, range 0.1-3.0) multiplies the cat's TURN_SPEED (4.25) — i.e. it tunes how fast A/D rotate the cat, which is the ONLY way to rotate the view. Adjustable via PauseMenu slider (persisted to localStorage) plus a separate moveSpeed multiplier.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.hpp:457, game/ui/MainMenu.cpp:112-125

> notes: Scope: SURVIVAL camera. Both codebases share art but have fundamentally different third-person camera paradigms.

LIVE (executed) constants — verified by reading, not config:
- Web camera (SurvivalScene, BasicScene.tsx:190-208): FOV 75, follow distance 10.5, height 8.4, lookAt(playerX, 0, playerZ), positioned from PLAYER rotation (welded behind cat), hard-snap every frame, NO mouse camera control. Three.js/drei defaults give near 0.1 / far ~2000. The GAME_CONFIG.PLAYER.CAMERA_DISTANCE=15 / CAMERA_HEIGHT=12 constants (gameConfig.ts:12-13) are DEAD — CameraFollow hardcodes 10.5/8.4 (=15*0.7 and 12*0.7).
- Native camera (human play, no --autoplay): FOV 60 (hardcoded CatAnnihilation.cpp:1575), offset (0,3,6)=6 back/3 up (PlayerControlSystem.hpp:418; setCameraOffset never called), lookAt player+0.75 torso, free mouse-look orbit (yaw/pitch, sens 0.002, pitch clamp [-1.4,+0.5]), lerped follow (speed 10), near 0.1 / far 2000. Adds camera-ground clamp, speed-bob, melee punch, kill shake.

The #1 parity gap (P1): native interactive play uses free mouse-orbit + camera-relative WASD strafe, while web uses tank-turn (A/D rotate cat) with the camera rigidly welded behind the cat's facing and NO mouse camera at all. Native's true web-equivalent (setFollowPlayerYaw, hard-snaps camera yaw to the cat's facing) is implemented but wired ONLY in the --autoplay CLI branch (main.cpp:833), so a normally-launched native game never gets the web camera behavior. To reach 1:1 for a human player, native needs: enable follow-player-yaw (or a tank-control locked-behind camera) by default in survival, remove/disable free mouse-look, raise FOV 60->75, and widen the offset from (0,3,6) toward web's 10.5-back / 8.4-up framing (with lookAt anchored to the terrain-adjusted equivalent of ground).

Confirmed no other camera wiring exists in CatAnnihilation.cpp (no setCameraOffset / setFollowPlayerYaw / setCinematicOrbit / setMouseSensitivity calls anywhere in game/ outside main.cpp's autoplay block).

Story-mode camera: StoryScene (BasicScene.tsx:213-251) reuses the identical CameraFollow (FOV 75, 10.5/8.4) — no separate story camera, so no additional story-only camera gap beyond the survival ones above.

### enemies-ai

- 🟡 **Chase / aggro engagement (enemies close on player)** [P1] — Native uses an Idle->Chasing state machine: updateIdleState only transitions to Chasing when distance <= aggroRange. But DogEntity::create OVERRIDES aggroRange to the per-type stat (DogEntity.cpp:361,391) = 15 (Dog/BigDog), 18 (FastDog), 25 (BossDog) — contradicting the EnemyComponent.hpp:38 default of 80 and its own comment ('generous so dogs always close regardless of spawn radius'). Meanwhile CatAnnihilation.cpp:208-209 spawns dogs at minSpawnDistance 25 to spawnRadius 40. So virtually every wave dog spawns 25-40m out with an aggro radius of 15-18m: it stays in AIState::Idle and never chases until the player walks within 15m of it. Web dogs relentlessly swarm from spawn; native dogs passively wait. In the survival arena this reads as broken enemies that ignore a stationary player.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:211: No aggro gating whatsoever — every enemy ALWAYS moves toward the player every frame while distance > ATTACK_RANGE (1.2). Enemies spawn at 8-15m and immediately swarm inward from the moment they appear. There is no 'idle/wait' state.  · native game/systems/EnemyAISystem.cpp:60-83
- 🟡 **Regular-dog movement speed** [P2] — Native regular Dog moveSpeed = 6.0 (also EnemyComponent.hpp:50) — 4x the web value of 1.5. Variants: BigDog 4.2, FastDog 9.0, BossDog 5.0 (DogEntity.cpp:395-421). Even accounting for native's faster player (10, CatEntity), a regular dog at 6 is 0.6x player speed vs web's 0.25x, so native dogs close much more aggressively per unit distance. Different absolute AND relative chase speed.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:109: ENEMY_SPEED = 1.5 units/s (matches GAME_CONFIG.ENEMY.SPEED, gameConfig.ts:19). With player MOVEMENT_SPEED 6 / RUN 12, the dog is 0.25x-0.125x of player speed — the player easily outruns them.  · native game/entities/DogEntity.cpp:389
- 🟡 **Regular-dog max health + per-wave HP scaling** [P2] — Native regular Dog base health = 50 (half of web's 100); per-variant: BigDog 100, FastDog 25, BossDog 300 (DogEntity.cpp:396,406,416). Wave scaling is multiplicative not additive: finalHealth = base * calculateHealthScaling(wave), where scaling = 1.0 + (wave-1)*0.1 plus a +/-0.15 cosine overlay (WaveDifficulty.hpp:136-144, healthScalingPerWave 0.1 default, NOT overridden in CatAnnihilation.cpp). So Dog HP wave1~=46, wave2~=57, wave3~=60 vs web 100/120/140. Native enemies have roughly half HP and a much flatter ~5-6 hp/wave growth vs web's +20/wave.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:552: Every enemy: totalHealth = baseHealth 100 + (currentWave-1)*20. Wave1=100, Wave2=120, Wave3=140... (GAME_CONFIG.ENEMY.BASE_HEALTH 100, HEALTH_PER_WAVE 20). All enemies identical HP regardless of anything but wave.  · native game/entities/DogEntity.cpp:386
- 🟡 **Wave enemy count formula** [P2] — Native routes through WaveDifficulty::calculateEnemyCount with config baseEnemyCount 3, enemyCountMultiplier 2.0 (CatAnnihilation.cpp:204-205) PLUS the default dense/sparse sine overlay (countAmplitude 2.0, period 3, WaveDifficulty.hpp:60-63). Actual counts: Wave1~=4, Wave2~=3, Wave3=7, Wave4~=10, Wave5~=9. The CatAnnihilation.cpp:205 comment claims '3/5/7/9/11' and WaveSystem finishes at wave 5 -> Victory. Web spawns nearly 2x more enemies per wave (7 vs 4 at wave 1) and ramps monotonically to unbounded waves, while native oscillates and caps the survival run at 5 waves.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:531: getEnemiesForWave(wave) = Math.floor((3 + wave*2) * 1.5). Wave1=7, Wave2=10, Wave3=13, Wave4=16, Wave5=19 (monotonic linear ramp). Matches GAME_CONFIG.WAVES base 3 / +2 per wave / x1.5.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:408-421
- ❌ **Enemy separation / flocking** [P2] — Native EnemyAISystem::updateChasingState only does moveTowardTarget + faceTarget with zero neighbor avoidance; there is no separation/flocking anywhere in the enemy system (grep confirms no separation logic in game/). Multiple dogs converging on the player will overlap/stack into the same point. Web dogs fan out around the player; native dogs pile up.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:195-208: Each enemy applies boid-style separation: for every other enemy within ENEMY_SEPARATION_RADIUS 1.5, add a push of (dir/dist)*separationStrength*SEPARATION_FORCE 3.0 to its movement (only while moving toward player). Keeps the pack visibly spread out instead of overlapping.  · native game/systems/EnemyAISystem.cpp:85-115
- 🟡 **Enemy spawn geometry (ring vs random)** [P2] — Native getSpawnPosition uses a fully random angle (uniform 0..2PI) and random radius uniform [minSpawnDistance 25, spawnRadius 40] (config from CatAnnihilation.cpp:208-209), then snaps Y to the terrain heightfield. So native spawns are (a) much farther out (25-40m vs 8-15m) and (b) randomly clustered rather than evenly ringed. The far spawn distance is what triggers the aggro-idle bug (see chase feature).
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:539-550: Evenly-spaced ring: angleStep = 2*PI / enemiesToSpawn, enemy i at angle i*angleStep, distance = MIN_SPAWN_DISTANCE 8 + rand*(SPAWN_DISTANCE 15 - 8), so 8-15m out, evenly distributed around the player at fixed y=0.5.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:376-405
- ❌ **Per-enemy floating health bar** [P2] — Native has NO per-enemy world-space health bar. HUD::renderHealthBar (HUD.cpp:362) is the PLAYER bar only; enemy feedback is a single screen-space 'Dogs remaining: N / M' counter (HUD.cpp:172-177,429-432) plus floating damage_numbers. A player cannot see an individual dog's remaining HP.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:483-495: Each enemy renders a world-space health bar group ~1.5 above it (dark backing box 1x0.08 + fill box scaled to healthPercent), billboarded to face the camera every frame (lines 391-395). Fill color shifts red/orange/dark-red by health%.  · native game/ui/HUD.cpp:172-177
- ❌ **Shield as physical barrier / directional block against enemies** [P2] — Native enemies have no concept of a shield barrier — updateAttackingState just applies attackDamage through HealthComponent::damage with no facing/shield check, and updateChasingState has no collision push-out against a player shield. Block/dodge exist in CombatSystem for the player's own defense but do not manifest as an enemy-facing physical wall or a directional attack-block the way the web enemy loop implements it.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:220-338: When a shield is equipped (slot 3 active), the enemy system builds a solid shield barrier 1.2 in front of the player (radius 0.9): enemy movement into it is zeroed and the enemy is pushed out, with a final post-move position-validation correction. Separately, an incoming enemy attack is blocked if the enemy is within 90 degrees of player facing (lines 356-375), and a player shield-bash deals 35 dmg + shoves the enemy back 3.0 units (lines 160-187).  · native game/systems/EnemyAISystem.cpp:117-178
- 🟡 **Regular-dog attack damage** [P2] — Native regular Dog attackDamage = 10 (also EnemyComponent.hpp:41,64). Per-variant: BigDog 15, FastDog 7.5, BossDog 25 (DogEntity.cpp:398,408,418). Regular dog hits for 10 vs web's 15.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:110: ATTACK_DAMAGE = 15 per hit (damagePlayer(15), line 372). Uniform across all enemies.  · native game/entities/DogEntity.cpp:388
- 🟡 **Regular-dog attack range** [P2] — Native regular Dog attackRange = 2.0 (EnemyComponent.hpp:39,40 default also 2.0). Per-variant: BigDog 2.5, FastDog 1.8, BossDog 3.0. Regular dog begins attacking from 2.0 out vs web's 1.2, so native dogs land hits from noticeably farther.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:111: ATTACK_RANGE = 1.2 — the enemy stops advancing and starts attacking within 1.2 units of the player.  · native game/entities/DogEntity.cpp:390
- 🟡 **Enemy attack cooldown** [P3] — Native attackCooldown = 1.2 s for ALL variants (EnemyComponent.hpp:42; DogEntity::create does NOT override it, so it stays 1.2 even for BossDog). 1.2s vs web 1.0s — dogs attack ~17% slower. Additionally native stamps a 0.2s invincibility window on the target after each dog hit (EnemyAISystem.cpp:172), a mechanic web lacks (web relies only on the per-enemy 1s cooldown).
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:112: ATTACK_COOLDOWN = 1000 ms between an enemy's attacks (checked via Date.now() - lastAttackTime, line 355).  · native game/components/EnemyComponent.hpp:42
- 🟡 **Enemy spawn stagger interval** [P3] — Native spawns one dog every spawnDelay = 1.5 s (WaveSystem::updateSpawning, WaveSystem.cpp:81-85), 7.5x slower than web's 0.2s. A wave visibly dribbles in over many seconds instead of appearing almost at once.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:568-596: All enemies for a wave are created up-front then revealed with setTimeout(index * 200 ms) — a fast trickle of ~5 dogs/second (GAME_CONFIG.WAVES.SPAWN_DELAY 200).  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:206
- ❌ **Enemy attack visual tell (scale pulse)** [P3] — Native dogs have no attack animation or scale pulse. Only idle/walk/run clips are marked looping and wired into the locomotion state machine (DogEntity.cpp:185-198); no 'attack'/'bite' clip is loaded or triggered in updateAttackingState. The dog deals damage with no visual tell (feedback is player-side camera shake + hit particles instead).
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:379-386: On each successful attack the enemy mesh scales to 1.3x for 200 ms then back to 1.0 — a quick lunge/pop that telegraphs the hit.  · native game/entities/DogEntity.cpp:185
- ❌ **Enemy body color darkens with health** [P3] — Native applies a FIXED per-variant tint override (Regular 0.55/0.40/0.25, Big dark brown, Fast grey, Boss red) that never changes with health. There is no health-driven color darkening; damage feedback is floating damage_numbers + hit particles instead of a body-color shift.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:399-400: enemyColor shifts by health%: >0.6 => #8B4513 (dirt brown), >0.3 => #654321, else #3E2723 (near-black) — the dog visibly darkens as it takes damage.  · native game/entities/DogEntity.cpp:225-240
- ✅ **Enemy face-player rotation** [P3] — faceTarget computes direction to target and calls transform->lookAt(targetPos, up) with an epsilon guard, in both chasing and attacking states. Behaviorally equivalent to the web atan2-to-player facing.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:289: rotation = Math.atan2(dx, dz) toward the player, written to groupRef.rotation.y each frame so the dog always looks at the player while chasing.  · native game/systems/EnemyAISystem.cpp:231-243
- 🟡 **Kill reward model (XP per kill)** [P3] — Native awards xpReward = enemy->scoreValue (Dog 10, FastDog 15, BigDog 25, BossDog 100; EnemyComponent/DogEntity) and publishes EnemyKilledEvent to LevelingSystem + a running score, rather than web's flat catXP 5. Different, type-weighted reward economy (native gives 2x-20x more per kill and varies by variant); web's per-weapon kill-XP split is not mirrored.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:637-651: On kill: addCatXP(5) flat for every enemy regardless of type, PLUS weapon kill XP of 15 to the weapon/element that landed the killing blow (10/8 per hit for sword/shield). No score concept.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:349
- 🔵 **Death handling (removal vs death animation)** [P3] — Native plays a 'layDown' death-pose clip (0.15s blend) and holds the corpse for kDeathPoseHoldSeconds 3.0 before HealthSystem reaps it (HealthSystem.cpp:30,209-212), plus a per-damage-type death particle burst + camera shake wired in CatAnnihilation. WaveSystem counts an isDead dog as already-defeated so the wave doesn't stall on the 3s corpse hold (WaveSystem.cpp:113-131). Net: native is a richer death sequence vs web's instant disappearance; neither side has loot drops.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:122-129: The instant health <= 0 the enemy is removed on the next frames: killNotifiedRef guards a single onKill, which filters it out of local state and splices it from globalCollisionData. No corpse, no death animation, no drop — it just vanishes.  · native game/systems/HealthSystem.cpp:209-212
- 🔵 **Enemy type variety (single vs four variants)** [P3] — Native ships 4 rigged Meshy GLB variants (Dog/BigDog/FastDog/BossDog) with distinct stats, scales (1.0/1.5/0.8/2.0), tints, and scores, spawned via a deterministic round-robin (slot%5 => Dog/Fast/Big/Dog/Dog) with BossDog forced every 5th wave (WaveSystem.cpp:268-286, isBossWave). This is added content beyond the web reference; the web's single generic dog maps only to native's regular Dog variant.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:402-497: Exactly ONE enemy: a brown box 'dog' built from primitives (body 0.6x0.5x1.2, head, snout, eyes, ears cones, 4 cylinder legs, tail, nose). Every wave enemy is this same mesh with identical stats — no big/fast/boss variants exist anywhere in the web code.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:266-286
- 🔵 **Boss wave cadence** [P3] — Native has isBossWave (every bossWaveInterval=5 waves) that forces all spawns to BossDog at 2.0x scale, and the survival run ends in Victory after clearing wave 5 (CatAnnihilation wave-complete handler). Native-only structure with no web equivalent.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:531: None. Web has no boss enemy and no boss-wave concept — waves are just larger counts of the same dog; the run continues indefinitely with no victory condition.  · native game/systems/WaveSystem.cpp:431-433

> notes: CONFIG SOURCE REALITY (must-know before comparing numbers): Web enemy constants are HARDCODED as local consts inside LocalEnemySystem.tsx (ENEMY_SPEED 1.5, ATTACK_DAMAGE 15, ATTACK_RANGE 1.2, ATTACK_COOLDOWN 1000, separation 1.5/3.0) — they happen to match gameConfig.ts GAME_CONFIG.ENEMY but the file does NOT import it, so gameConfig.ts is documentation, not the live source. Native has THREE partly-dead constant sources: (1) game/config/GameplayConfig.hpp and BalanceConfig.hpp enemy taxonomies are NOT used by the dog path at all; (2) EnemyComponent.hpp's constructor sets per-type stats but is then OVERWRITTEN by (3) DogEntity::getStatsForType (DogEntity.cpp:381-427), which is the ACTUAL live per-variant stat table for wave-spawned dogs. Wave tuning is the WaveConfig override in CatAnnihilation.cpp:203-210 (base 3, mult 2.0, spawnDelay 1.5, transitionDelay 5.0, minSpawnDistance 25, spawnRadius 40) — but healthScalingPerWave (0.1) and the dense/sparse sine overlay (countAmplitude 2.0/period 3) are left at WaveDifficulty defaults, so the '3/5/7/9/11' comment on CatAnnihilation.cpp:205 is stale — the real counts are ~4/3/7/10/9.

THE STANDOUT BUG (feature #1, P1): DogEntity::create sets each dog's aggroRange to the per-type stat (15/18/25) which is SMALLER than the wave spawn distance (25-40m), so wave-spawned dogs sit in AIState::Idle and never chase a stationary player — directly contradicting EnemyComponent.hpp:38's aggroRange=80 'always close regardless of spawn radius' intent. Web has no aggro gate and swarms from spawn. Cheapest 1:1 fixes: raise per-type aggroRange above spawnRadius (e.g. >=45) OR reduce spawn distance to web's 8-15m; the latter also fixes the spawn-geometry gap.

engine/ai/ (BehaviorTree.cpp, AISystem.cpp, Navigation.cpp, Blackboard.cpp) is a full behavior-tree + navmesh AI library but is NOT wired to the dogs — grep confirms it's referenced only within engine/ai/ itself. The dogs run entirely on the hand-rolled game/systems/EnemyAISystem 4-state machine. So the fancy engine AI is unused portfolio infra, irrelevant to actual enemy behavior parity.

No loot/drops on either side. Web's GAME_CONFIG.PERFORMANCE.MAX_ENEMIES 50 is never enforced in LocalEnemySystem (dead config). All web enemy behavior reviewed is live (none commented out).

### player-movement

- 🟡 **Movement control scheme (tank vs camera-relative)** [P1] — Native is camera-relative: WASD build an inputDirection (W:z-=1, S:z+=1, A:x-=1, D:x+=1) that is rotated by cameraYaw and fed to applyMovement, then the player is auto-rotated to FACE the movement direction (atan2(moveDir.x,-moveDir.z), cpp:173-182). So native A/D STRAFE and the cat auto-turns toward travel, whereas web A/D TURN and W/S are locked to facing. A player notices immediately: web feels like tank/RuneScape steering, native feels like a modern twin-stick/third-person shooter.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:280-297: Tank controls: W adds x+=sin(rotation)*speed, z+=cos(rotation)*speed (forward relative to the cat's own facing); S subtracts (backward). A/D do NOT strafe — they rotate the cat. Movement is purely along the cat's current facing axis. No camera-relative strafing exists.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:132-186
- ❌ **Player turn/rotation via A/D keys (TURN_SPEED 4.25 rad/s)** [P1] — Native has no key-driven turn. A/D are strafe axes; the cat's rotation is set implicitly by the movement-direction auto-face (cpp:176). There is no TURN_SPEED constant and no way to pivot in place with keys. Web players who hold A/D to spin the cat get lateral sliding instead.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:280-285: A adds to rotation, D subtracts, at rotationSpeed = GAME_CONFIG.PLAYER.TURN_SPEED (4.25 rad/s, gameConfig.ts:11) * delta * spinSensitivity (default 1.0). Facing is driven ENTIRELY by A/D key-held turning; the camera follows the resulting rotation. On mobile the turn rate is cut to 30% (index.tsx:271).  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:149-152
- 🟡 **Walk speed 6 u/s and run speed 12 u/s** [P2] — Native player is created with moveSpeed 12 (createCustom, CatAnnihilation.cpp:2520) — equal to the web RUN speed — with maxSpeed 24. There is only ONE speed tier; no distinct 6 u/s walk exists, and there is no sprint multiplier applied (see Sprint feature). Net: the native cat always moves at web-sprint velocity with no slower walk, so pacing/feel differs.
  - web src/config/gameConfig.ts:9-10: PLAYER.MOVEMENT_SPEED = 6, PLAYER.RUN_SPEED = 12. Applied as speed = 6 * delta * moveSpeedMultiplier (index.tsx:257); running multiplies by runMultiplier = RUN_SPEED/MOVEMENT_SPEED = 2.0 (index.tsx:256,267). So walk = 6 units/s, run = 12 units/s, two distinct tiers.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2520
- ❌ **Sprint on Shift (2x speed)** [P2] — Native binds Shift to HEAVY ATTACK modifier (shiftHeld -> attackType 'H', cpp:308-316), not sprint. processMovementInput applies no sprint multiplier and GameplayConfig.Player.SPRINT_MULTIPLIER (1.5, GameplayConfig.hpp:23) is never read. There is no sprint at all, and Shift does something entirely different — a web player pressing Shift to run instead triggers heavy attacks.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:266-268: Holding Shift sets controlsActive.run and multiplies speed by runMultiplier (2.0), and sets player.isRunning true (index.tsx:175-178) which switches the run animation. Shift is the sprint key.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:308-316
- 🟡 **Instant (non-accelerated) movement integration** [P2] — Native uses a velocity model with acceleration 50 and deceleration 30 (MovementComponent set in CatEntity.cpp:114-115 / overridden in createPlayer), lerping horizontalVelocity toward desiredVelocity (applyMovement) and bleeding off via applyDeceleration when input stops, clamped to maxSpeed 24. Result: native has ramp-up/ramp-down inertia where web snaps instantly — a perceptibly different movement feel.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:439: Movement is applied directly to position each frame: x/z += sin/cos(rotation)*speed with speed already = baseSpeed*delta, then setPlayerPosition({x,y,z,rotation}). No velocity, no acceleration or deceleration — the cat reaches full speed and stops instantly.  · native game/components/MovementComponent.hpp:42-91
- 🔵 **No mouse-look camera (web camera is rotation-driven only)** [P1] — Native processMouseLook consumes mouse delta into cameraYaw (yaw) and cameraPitch (pitch) at mouseSensitivity 0.002 (hpp:457), clamped pitch [-1.4, 0.5] rad, for human play (followPlayerYaw is only turned on under --autoplay, main.cpp:833). So a native human player has a free-orbiting mouse camera decoupled from cat facing, which does not exist in web at all — the two camera control models are fundamentally different.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:138-160: The web game reads NO mouse movement for camera control. Mouse is used only for click attacks (index.tsx:199-222). The camera (CameraFollow) is derived purely from the player's rotation each frame. There is no free-look, no pitch control, no mouse sensitivity for the camera.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:242-278
- 🟡 **Camera locked behind player by facing (dist 10.5, height 8.4, hard snap)** [P1] — Native cameraOffset default is (0, 3.0, 6.0) (hpp:418) with lerp smoothing at cameraFollowSpeed 10 (cpp:912-917), plus camera bob and attack-punch. The behind-the-cat 'follow player yaw' hard-snap that mirrors web (cpp:833-868) is ONLY enabled in --autoplay; a human game leaves the free mouse camera. Framing differs (6 back / 3 up vs 10.5 back / 8.4 up), smoothing differs (lerp vs snap), and human native does not sit behind the cat at all. setCameraOffset is never called to match web's (0,12,15)-derived rig.
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:142-157: CameraFollow every frame: cameraX = x - sin(rotation)*10.5, cameraZ = z - cos(rotation)*10.5, cameraY = 8.4, then lookAt(x,0,z). Distance 10.5 (comment: 15*0.7), height 8.4 (12*0.7). Hard snap (no smoothing). Camera is always directly behind the cat's facing.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:786-917
- 🟡 **Attack on Spacebar and Left-click (sword)** [P2] — Native Left-click attacks (processAttackInput, cpp:306), matching web's left-click, but Spacebar is bound to JUMP (processJumpInput -> movement->jump(), cpp:287-289), not attack. A web player pressing Space to swing the sword instead triggers a (neutralized) jump in native. Attack-input binding is only half-aligned.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:179-182: Spacebar (with e.preventDefault) calls performAttack(); Left mouse button (button 0) also calls performAttack (index.tsx:199-203). performAttack (index.tsx:150-165) sets isAttacking true for 300ms only if the active hotbar item id === 'sword'. Space is the primary attack key.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:280-318
- 🟡 **Shield bash on Right-click (slot-gated)** [P2] — Native Right-click is bound to BLOCK (processBlockInput -> combatSystem_->startBlock/endBlock, cpp:326-332) — a hold-to-block defensive stance, not a slot-gated shield-bash attack. Different action and no inventory-slot gating. (Combat-domain overlap, but the input binding lives in player control.)
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:204-213: Right mouse button (button 2) triggers performAttack ONLY if inventory slot 3 holds a 'shield' and activeSlot === 3 — a shield bash reusing the attack path. Context menu is suppressed (index.tsx:225-227).  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:320-333
- 🟡 **Jump (none in web — cat stays grounded, Space reserved for attack)** [P3] — Native has a full jump mechanic wired (jumpForce 15, gravity -30 m/s^2, MovementComponent.jump()), but it is deliberately neutralized in survival by an UNCONDITIONAL per-frame ground snap to the terrain height (cpp:211-219 / 662-670), so the cat cannot leave the ground. Net grounded behavior matches web, but native reserves Space for jump (vs web's attack) and carries dead jump/gravity code the web lacks.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:274: The cat is always grounded: y is hardcoded to 0 in the move loop (const y = 0, index.tsx:274), only overridden by bridge/ramp heights in story. isJumping exists in the store (gameStore.ts:53) and is passed to the mesh but Controls never calls setPlayerJumping — there is no jump mechanic; Space is the attack key.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:194-219
- 🟡 **Ground stick to flat y=0 plane (survival)** [P2] — Native snaps the cat's Y to a CUDA Perlin heightmap sample (terrain_->getHeightAt(x,z)) every frame, so the native cat walks over rolling uneven terrain while the web survival cat is pinned to a flat y=0 plane. Ground-stick logic exists on both, but the surface it sticks to differs (flat vs heightfield) — a visible movement/verticality difference.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:274: In SurvivalScene the cat walks on a flat plane: y is forced to 0 every frame (finalY starts at y=0). TerrainCollisionSystem is NOT mounted in survival (BasicScene.tsx:190-208 mounts no terrain collision), so terrainCollisionData.rivers/bridges are empty — no height variation, the ground is perfectly flat at y=0.  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:211-219
- 🔵 **Obstacle / tree collision push-out** [P2] — Native adds pushOutOfTrees() every frame: for each of ~18,931 Forest tree colliders within a 4m search radius, if dist < treeRadius(0.5*scale*{Pine0.8/Oak1.2/Bush0.6}) + playerRadius(0.5) it pushes the cat radially to the circle edge. This makes native trees solid obstacles, which the web survival mode does not have — a divergence (native is arguably more correct, but it is behavior the reference lacks in survival).
  - web src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx:198: In SurvivalScene the trees are ForestEnvironment decorations with NO collision — the cat walks straight through them. Survival has no tree/static-object push-out at all (TerrainCollisionSystem, which does static-object push, is only mounted in StoryScene, BasicScene.tsx:239).  · native game/systems/PlayerControlSystem.cpp:728-784
- ❌ **River/water predictive collision (buffer 2.0)** [P3] — story-mode: Native has no river/water body and no water-block movement logic. Only relevant when story mode returns; not part of the survival 1:1 target.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx:299-330: Story-mode: before committing a move, iterate terrainCollisionData.rivers; if the target x/z is within (river bounds expanded by waterBuffer 2.0), and not on a bridge, cancel the move and revert to previous position — a predictive block so the cat cannot enter water. - ✅ **Spawn position at world origin** [P3] — Native spawns at (0, terrain->getHeightAt(0,0), 0) with identity rotation (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2508-2512). - 🟡 **Player cat model (procedural primitives vs Meshy GLB)** [P2] — Native loads a rigged Meshy GLB (assets/models/cats/rigged/ember_leader.glb) with a skeleton, tinted ember-orange (tintOverride (1.0,0.504,0.224), CatEntity.cpp:173-174). - 🟡 **Locomotion animation states (idle/walk/run)** [P2] — Native drives real skeletal clips through wireLocomotionTransitions with speed thresholds (idle->walk 1.0, walk->idle 0.5, walk->run 6.0, run->walk 5.0, 0.2s blend) fed by MovementComponent.getCurrentSpeed(), configured in CatEntity.cpp:257-338. Architecturally richer, but (a) the trigger model differs (continuous speed vs booleans), and (b) CPU skinning is OFF by default (--no-cpu-skinning default per main.cpp), leaving the cat in bind-pose (a known 'cat on its back' bug), so the native cat frequently shows NO locomotion animation at all — a visible regression vs web's always-animated procedural cat.
  - web src/components/game/CatCharacter/CatMesh.tsx:166-213: Procedural, driven by isMoving/isRunning booleans: walk cycle sin(walkTime) with animSpeed 5 (walk) or 10 (run); head bob (±0.1 walk / ±0.15 run), tail wag (speed 2/3, amount 0.2/0.3), body y held at 0.2; idle does a slow tail swish (sin*0.1). > notes: Dominant gap is the control SCHEME, not tuning: web = tank controls (A/D rotate the cat at TURN_SPEED 4.25 rad/s, W/S move along facing, Shift=sprint 2x, Space=attack, camera hard-locked behind the cat's rotation at 10.5 back / 8.4 up, NO mouse-look); native = camera-relative strafe (WASD relative to camera yaw, cat auto-faces movement, free mouse-look yaw/pitch at sens 0.002, Shift=heavy-attack, Space=jump, camera offset (0,3,6) with lerp+bob+punch). The behind-the-cat follow-yaw that would approximate web only turns on under --autoplay, never in human play (main.cpp:833) — so a human native session plays nothing like the web reference. Achieving 1:1 requires: (1) re-implement A/D as in-place turn with TURN_SPEED 4.25 and W/S as facing-relative move, (2) disable mouse-look and enable follow-player-yaw for human play with cameraOffset matching web's 10.5-back/8.4-up rig, (3) add a 6 u/s walk tier with Shift=2x sprint, (4) rebind Space to attack (web has no functional jump), (5) decide whether to keep native-only additions (dodge, tree collision in survival, camera bob/punch) or strip them for strict parity.\n\nConstant/config caveat (META): the web player speeds live in GAME_CONFIG (6/12) but native player stats are HARDCODED in CatAnnihilation::createPlayer (moveSpeed 12, maxHealth 400, attackDamage 60, attackSpeed 3, attackRange 4, CatAnnihilation.cpp:2518-2525), which OVERRIDE both GameplayConfig.hpp (BASE_SPEED 8) and BalanceConfig.hpp (MOVE_SPEED 5) and CatEntity's DEFAULT_MOVE_SPEED 10 — none of the three native config sources is the live value for the player. Verify against createPlayer, not the config headers.\n\nSkinning bug compounds the animation gap: native locomotion clips are wired correctly (LocomotionStateMachine thresholds idle/walk/run) but CPU skinning defaults OFF (--no-cpu-skinning), so the native cat renders in bind pose ('on its back') with no visible walk/run animation — a P1-visible regression against the web's always-animated procedural cat, folded into the F17 locomotion-animation entry.\n\nSurvival scope: rivers/bridges/ramps (F13/F14) are story-mode only and inert in the web SurvivalScene; native has no equivalents but they are out of the survival 1:1 target. Tree collision (F12) is the opposite — web survival has NONE (decorative trees) while native makes ~18,931 trees solid; that is a real divergence to reconcile.

### environment

- 🟡 **Ground plane geometry & size** [P3] — Native ground is the CUDA Terrain mesh force-flattened to y=0 (std::fill heightmap = 0, normals forced (0,1,0)), but the terrain is only 512x512 world units (GameWorld Config worldSize=512, halfSize 256) vs web's 10000x10000. Player is hard-clamped to +/-256 (GameWorld::clampToBounds) while web is effectively unbounded. Fog far=150 hides the edge in most frames, so the size delta is rarely visible, but the world bound is a real mechanical difference. Ground sits at y=0 vs web y=-0.1 (negligible).
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:306-315: Flat MeshStandardMaterial plane, planeGeometry args [10000, 10000], rotated -PI/2 on X, positioned at (0, -0.1, 0), receiveShadow. Base color #7fb069, roughness 0.9, metalness 0. Effectively unbounded playfield (10000x10000 units).  · native game/world/Terrain.cpp:273; game/world/GameWorld.hpp:26
- ✅ **Procedural grass diffuse texture** [P3] — Native GenerateGrassTexture mirrors the algorithm exactly (base #7fb069, 300 blades rgb(127±10,176±10,105) height 2..5, 15 dark spots rgba(45,80,50,128) radius 1..4), 256x256 RGBA8, TileSize=500. scene.frag samples uv=worldPos.xz/500 with REPEAT so world-space tile scale matches. Only difference: native uses a fixed seed (0xCA75A55) for reproducible screenshots vs web's per-load randomness — same visual character, different exact pixels.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:241-293: 256x256 canvas: base fill #7fb069; 300 grass-blade rects fillRect(x,y,1, rand*4+2) in rgb(127±10, 176±10, 105); 15 dark spots rgba(45,80,50,0.5) filled circles radius rand*3+1. CanvasTexture, RepeatWrapping, repeat.set(20,20) over the 10000 plane => 500 world units per tile. Re-randomized every page load.  · native game/world/GrassTexture.cpp:59-158; shaders/scene/scene.frag:98-103
- ✅ **Tree primitive geometry (pine/oak trunk + foliage)** [P3] — Native BuildProceduralTreeMeshes generates identical geometry: trunk cylinder top 0.3 bottom 0.4 height 4 radialSegs 8 at yCentre 2; pine foliage sphere r=2 12x12 at (0,5,0); oak foliage sphere r=2.5 12x12 at (0,5,0). Colors matched in the draw loop: trunk #654321 (0.396,0.263,0.129), foliage #228B22 (0.133,0.545,0.133) (CatAnnihilation.cpp:1861-1862). Geometry and color are 1:1.

- 🟡 **Rendered tree count / on-screen density** [P2] — Native Forest generates thousands of trees (Poisson-disk, minDistance 3 over 512x512 => ~18.9k instances) but the render loop hard-caps visible trees to kTreeDrawBudget=16 within an 18m horizontal cull (kTreeDistanceCullMetres=18) plus a 12m spawn-exclusion around origin. Result: at most a tight ring of ~16 trees near the player vs web's ~163 filling the mid/far field. Visibly far sparser tree presence. Root cause is no GPU instancing yet (per-tree draw cost). Tuned down deliberately after a 'wayyyy too many trees' playtest.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:369-421: ~163 trees ALL rendered simultaneously: 100 random-ring trees (dist 20..220) + ~63 grid trees (grid -300..300 step 80, skip cells within 50 of center). No culling/budget — every tree is in the scene graph and drawn.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:1783-1786
- 🟡 **Tree placement distribution** [P3] — Native uses Poisson-disk sampling (uniform natural scatter, minDistance 3) across the whole 512x512 terrain rather than a ring+grid+center-cutout scheme. The distributions differ in character (even organic scatter vs concentric ring plus jittered grid), and the central clear zone is enforced at render time (12m origin exclusion) rather than at generation. Same order of visual 'forest scattered around player' but not the same placement pattern.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:369-421: Two deterministic passes: (1) 100 trees at angle=rand*2PI, distance=20+rand*200 (ring around player); (2) grid loop x,z in [-300,300] step 80 with +/-20 jitter, skipping the central sqrt(x^2+z^2)<50 cutout to keep spawn area clear.  · native game/world/Forest.cpp:64-201
- 🟡 **Tree scale range** [P3] — Native Forest::Params minScale=0.8 maxScale=1.3 (scaleDist 0.8..1.3), so native trees are uniformly larger (min 0.8, up to 1.3) than web (0.4..1.0). Combined with the identical base geometry this makes each native tree read bigger than its web counterpart.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:380,410: Ring trees scale 0.5 + rand*0.5 (0.5..1.0); grid trees scale 0.4 + rand*0.6 (0.4..1.0). Trees are generally smaller-to-full size.  · native game/world/Forest.hpp:74-75
- 🟡 **Tree type ratio (pine vs oak)** [P3] — Native selectTreeType uses pineRatio 0.5 / oakRatio 0.3 / bushRatio 0.2. - ❌ **Tree wind sway animation** [P3] — Native trees are fully static — modelMatrix = translate(pos) * rotateY(tree.rotation) * scale, with a fixed per-instance rotation and no per-frame sway term. No wind animation is applied to tree transforms. Distant forest is motionless where web trees gently sway.
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:142-153: Each tree sways every frame via useFrame: rotation.x = sin(animOffset + elapsedTime*0.5) * 0.01; rotation.z = cos((animOffset + t)*0.7) * 0.01. - 🟡 **Distance fog (color/model/range)** [P3] — Native terrain fog matches exactly: FOG_COLOR #4c6156 (76/255,97/255,86/255), linear, FOG_NEAR 30, FOG_FAR 150, horizontal-distance based (scene.frag). - 🟡 **Sky / background color** [P3] — Native swapchain clear is (0.50,0.72,0.95) and it additionally renders a full-screen sky-gradient shader each frame (zenith->horizon smoothstep + warm sun halo, day-cycle-interpolated DAWN/MIDDAY/DUSK presets; MIDDAY horizon = 0.50,0.72,0.95). - 🟡 **Directional (sun) light** [P3] — Native SUN_DIR = normalize(0.35,0.85,0.4) (~60deg elevation, higher/more overhead than web's ~45deg) and SUN_COLOR = (1.0,0.96,0.88) warm tungsten white vs web's pure white intensity 1. - 🔵 **Tree collision (walk-through vs blocked)** [P2] — Native adds a static physics collider per Forest tree (~18.9k sphere colliders sized by type: pine radius*0.8 height*1.5, oak radius*1.2, bush radius*0.6) and PlayerControlSystem pushes the cat out of trees. So in native trees physically block/push the player, while in web they are pass-through decor. A player would immediately feel the movement difference. (Belongs partly to collision-physics domain but is an environment-driven behavior delta.)
  - web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx:340-492: In survival, ForestEnvironment trees/bushes/rocks are purely visual — no collider, no collision system references them. The player cat walks straight through trees; scenery never blocks movement.  · native game/world/GameWorld.cpp:202-247

> notes: Domain: environment/scene for SURVIVAL mode (story terrain SimpleTerrainSystem is out of scope per user directive + parity spec 01). Reviewed both sides in full: web src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx + BasicScene.tsx SurvivalScene; native game/world/{Terrain,Forest,ProceduralTreeMesh,GrassTexture,Environment,GameWorld}, shaders/scene/{scene.frag,entity.frag}, shaders/sky/sky_gradient.frag, engine/renderer/Renderer.cpp + passes/ScenePass.cpp, and the tree/terrain submission loop in game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:1440-1959.

CONSTANTS-ACTUALLY-EXECUTED caveat (matches the enumeration's config-reconciliation warning): none of GameplayConfig/BalanceConfig/GameWorld default-config numbers drive the visible environment — the live values are hardcoded in the shaders (scene.frag/entity.frag/sky_gradient.frag), Renderer.cpp clear color, GrassTexture.cpp, ProceduralTreeMesh.cpp, Forest::Params, and the CatAnnihilation render loop (cull 18m / budget 16). The Environment class (fog default 0.7,0.8,0.9 start50 end300; ambient 0.3,0.3,0.4; weather; wind) is constructed but NOT wired into the survival render path — treat it as dormant scaffolding, not the source of truth for what renders.

Highest-leverage gaps for 1:1: (P2) rocks entirely missing; (P2) on-screen tree density 16 vs ~163; (P2) no real-time shadows; (P2) trees are solid colliders in native but pass-through in web. Everything else (grass texture, tree/bush geometry+color, fog color/range on ground) is at or near parity. The single closest match is the grass texture (algorithm ported constant-for-constant) and tree/bush primitive geometry+colors.

Web ground is flat and unbounded (10000); native is flat (Perlin force-zeroed) but bounded to 512 (player clamped +/-256). Native sky is a per-frame gradient+halo+day-cycle vs web's flat #87CEEB — an enhancement that is not a literal color match. Entity vs terrain fog target color is inconsistent in native (entities/trees -> sky blue 0.50,0.72,0.95; ground -> #4c6156), where web fogs everything to #4c6156.

### progression

- 🟡 **Cat XP awarded per enemy kill** [P2] — Native awards cat XP = EnemyComponent.scoreValue per kill, which is PER-TYPE: Dog 10, FastDog 15, BigDog 25, BossDog 100 (EnemyComponent.hpp:53-84) — not a flat 5. Because native has 4 dog variants this is arguably richer, but the base value (10 vs web's 5) and per-type scaling both differ. Separately, native's declared EnemyXPRewards table (10/25/50/100/500, xp_tables.hpp:118-124) is UNUSED — scoreValue wins. Kill XP is wired and reaches LevelingSystem::addXP, but see the next rows: the resulting level-ups have no gameplay effect.
  - web src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx:639: On every kill, killEnemy() calls addCatXP(5) — a FLAT 5 cat-XP per kill regardless of enemy (web has only one dog type). GAME_CONFIG.EXPERIENCE.ENEMY_KILL_XP=5 (gameConfig.ts:79). Note: the store's incrementEnemiesKilled() (gameStore.ts:723, also grants 5) is dead — never called; addCatXP is the sole live path.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:3305
- 🟡 **Cat level XP curve + max level** [P2] — Native uses a hardcoded CAT_XP_TABLE = 100*1.5^(level-1) (100,150,225,340,500,...) and hard-caps the cat at level 50 (leveling_system.cpp:74/80). Completely different curve shape AND a different cap (50 vs 99). Also note native's addXP SUBTRACTS xpToNextLevel on level-up (running remainder, leveling_system.cpp:81) whereas web keeps cumulative total XP and compares against an absolute threshold — different XP-accounting model.

Different mechanism (explicit slots/Continue vs web's automatic single-key localStorage) and native does not persist per-weapon-skill XP (weapon skills reset each session) nor a survival high-score triple. Both retain cat level/XP, so partial.

> notes: Overarching finding: the native LevelingSystem (leveling_system.cpp/.hpp + xp_tables.hpp) is a complete, well-documented progression engine, but it is almost entirely DORMANT in the survival loop. Only ONE wire is live — enemy kills call levelingSystem_->addXP(scoreValue) (CatAnnihilation.cpp:3305) and wave-complete adds XP (3652). Everything downstream of leveling is disconnected: (1) LevelUpEvent is subscribed (856) but never published and setLevelUpCallback is never called, so the onLevelUp handler that would scale player max HP (+10) and full-heal NEVER runs → native player max HP is pinned at 100 all game; (2) applyRegeneration, canRevive/useRevive (Nine Lives), getEffectiveSpeed/getDodgeSpeedMultiplier/hasDoubleJump (Agility), getCritMultiplier (Alpha Strike), canSeeEnemyDetails (Predator Instinct), and addWeaponXP/getWeaponDamageMultiplier (weapon skills) are all implemented but never called from any live system; (3) the HUD shows no level/XP/abilities. The two P1 gaps for survival parity are therefore: level-up max-HP scaling (web +20/level, functional; native missing) and Nine Lives revive (web 30% functional; native 50% but unwired).

Important nuance on the WEB reference: several 'level rewards' are themselves non-functional in the live web build. Regeneration (2 HP/s), Agility (1.25x speed), Predator Instinct (enemy HP bars), and Alpha Strike (crit) are all set/displayed on level-up but their constants are never consumed by any system — so on the web side only +20 max HP/level and Nine Lives (30% revive) actually do anything. resetNineLives() is also never called, making web Nine Lives once-per-game rather than the documented once-per-wave. Sword is the only weapon whose damage scales with its skill level (40+(lvl-1)*10); bow/magic skills level up cosmetically. These web dead-effects mean a strict 1:1 port would replicate mostly-cosmetic abilities — worth confirming with the owner whether the TARGET is the web's live behavior or its intended behavior before wiring the native equivalents.

Key constant deltas captured: kill XP web flat 5 vs native per-type 10/15/25/100; cat curve web floor(sum floor(i+500*2^(i/6))/5.4) cap 99 vs native 100*1.5^(n-1) cap 50; HP/level web +20 vs native +10; Nine Lives revive web 30% vs native 50%; weapon cap web 99 vs native 20 (elemental 15); base max HP 100 on both.

- ❌ **Nine Lives death-interception (survive death once per wave)** [P2] — Native LevelingSystem unlocks a 'nineLives' ability (parity in the leveling/ability set), but the native death path (HealthSystem death callback -> setState(GameOver), CatAnnihilation.cpp:373-375) contains no revive interception -- a killing blow always transitions to GameOver regardless of the nineLives unlock. The web's revive-at-30%-once-per-wave mechanic is not wired into native death handling. (Ability unlock itself overlaps combat-abilities; the death-flow interception is the gameflow gap.)
  - web src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:677-687: Inside damagePlayer, if the blow would kill AND catStats.abilities.nineLives (unlocked at cat level 15) AND !nineLivesUsed -> death is cancelled: player revives at floor(maxHealth*0.3) (30% HP), nineLivesUsed=true, isGameOver stays false (gameStore.ts:677-687). resetNineLives() clears nineLivesUsed (per-wave). This directly intercepts the death->gameover flow.  · native game/systems/leveling_system.hpp
- 🟡 **Restart / Try Again flow** [P3] — Native restart() is in-place: ecs_.clearEntities(), reset gameTime/enemiesKilled/waveNumber to 0, reset day/night to noon (0.5), recreate player, repopulate NPCs, setState(Playing) (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2248-2273). Reachable from GameOver via R/Enter/Space (updateGameOver, 2071-2075) and from Victory via Enter/Space (2086-2089). Functionally equivalent to web's 'Try Again', but native resets to wave 1 (or --starting-wave N) live while web does a hard reload; native persists no cross-run progression into the restart (see persistence).
  - web src/components/ui/GameOverScreen.tsx:29-47: 'Try Again' button or Space/Enter calls handleRestart = window.location.reload() (GameOverScreen.tsx:30-31,38-46) -- a full page reload. Because gameMode + player progress persist in localStorage, the reload lands back into survival with cat level/xp/weapon-skills restored and waves/enemies reset.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2248-2273
- ✅ **Quit to menu / mode-selection** [P3] — Native quitToMenu() clears entities, resets gameTime/enemiesKilled/waveNumber, isStoryMode_=false, setState(MainMenu) (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2314-2328); wired to PauseMenu 'Main Menu' button (600-602) and to Q/Esc in GameOver/Victory. Behaviour matches, except web returns to the mode+customization chooser while native returns to a plain Start/Continue main menu.
  - web src/components/ui/PauseMenu.tsx:59-76: Pause menu 'Quit Game' (handleQuitGame) sets gameMode=null and storyMode.isActive=false, then resets isGameOver/isPaused/currentWave(1)/isWaveTransition/enemiesKilled (PauseMenu.tsx:60-75). This makes GameModeSelection re-appear (App.tsx gate), returning to mode+customization selection.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2314-2328
- 🟡 **Progress persistence model (save/load)** [P2] — Native uses an explicit multi-slot SaveSystem: saveGame(slot) serializes level/xp, health, position+rotation, activeQuests, completedQuests, storyState{chapter,mission}, timeOfDay, currentDay, currency (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2334-2412); loadGame restores them (2414-2498); Continue picks the most-recent slot (2288-2312). BUT CatAnnihilation::saveGame() is never called anywhere in game code (no Save button, no autosave call site -- MAX_AUTOSAVE_FILES exists only as a config constant), so saves are effectively never written and Continue has nothing to load. Content deltas: native persists position/rotation/currency/timeOfDay (web doesn't); web persists weaponSkills, survivalHighScore, clan appearance, storySkills, clanRelationships, mysticalConnections (native doesn't). Trigger model differs entirely (web=continuous autosave, native=manual-but-unwired slots).
  - web src/lib/store/gameStatePersistence.ts:164-186: Automatic localStorage persistence, 3 keys (gameStatePersistence.ts:7-11): 'game-mode'; 'story-progress' (isActive, playerClan, playerRank, mentorName, activeQuests, completedQuests, storySkills, clanRelationships, territoryAccess, mysticalConnections); 'player-progress' (catLevel, catXp, weaponSkills object, survivalHighScore{wave,enemiesKilled,survivalTime}). Saved continuously on progression events (savePlayerProgress inside addCatXP gameStore.ts:911; saveStoryProgress on clan/rank/quest/story-xp actions). Restored on store creation (createInitialState, gameStore.ts:598-630).  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2334-2498
- ❌ **Survival high-score tracking** [P2] — Native has no high-score / best-wave persistence; SaveGameData carries no survival-record fields, and per-session enemiesKilled_/waveNumber_ reset on every restart with nothing tracking a personal best. No native equivalent to the web survivalHighScore.
  - web src/lib/store/gameStatePersistence.ts:177-181: player-progress persists survivalHighScore = { wave: max(prev,currentWave), enemiesKilled: max(prev,enemiesKilled), survivalTime: max(prev,survivalTimeSeconds) } (gameStatePersistence.ts:177-181), monotonically tracking bests across runs. GameModeSelection advertises 'Leaderboards coming soon' (GameModeSelection.tsx:361).
- ❌ **Reset-all-progress control** [P3] — Native has no reset-progress UI or action. (It is somewhat moot because native saves are never written, but there is no equivalent affordance to wipe stored state.)
  - web src/components/ui/GameModeSelection.tsx:35-43: A 'Reset Progress' button on the mode-selection screen uses a two-click confirm ('Click again to confirm', 3s timeout) then calls clearAllProgress() (removes all 3 localStorage keys) and window.location.reload() (GameModeSelection.tsx:35-43,417-425; clearAllProgress gameStatePersistence.ts:191-196).
- ✅ **Wave-transition state/overlay** [P3] — Native models a WaveComplete state in GameUI's GameState enum (GameUI.hpp:27) with a WavePopup ('Wave X Complete!' + next-wave preview stats). Both show an inter-wave transition. (Detailed wave cadence/timing constants -- spawnDelay 1.5s, transitionDelay 5s -- belong to the waves domain; this entry only notes the flow-state's presence on both sides.)
  - web src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:212: isWaveTransition flag (gameStore.ts:212, setWaveTransition) plus a non-Zustand WaveState pub/sub (WaveState.ts) drive a 'Wave Complete / Next Wave' staggered overlay (WaveTransition.tsx) rendered outside the Canvas between waves.  · native game/ui/GameUI.hpp:27
- 🟡 **Story mode systems cluster (NPCs / dialog / quests / ranks / skills)** [P3] — story-mode. Native has the full cluster of systems -- StoryModeSystem (Clan, ClanRank ladder, chapters/missions), QuestSystem (QuestType Main/Side/Daily, quest_data.hpp catalogue), DialogSystem (dialog trees + variable substitution), NPCSystem (mentors/leaders/merchants), story_skills, clan_territory, MerchantSystem -- all registered (CatAnnihilation.hpp:578-587). But the whole cluster is unreachable in survival: NPCs are disabled in survival, story mode is not startable from the menu, and native models chapters/missions rather than web's individual quest-object graph, so the two quest data models don't line up 1:1. Structure exists on both sides; the flow entry point and data-shape differ.
  - web src/lib/store/gameStore.ts:180-195: story-mode. storyMode state (gameStore.ts:180-195) holds playerClan, playerRank (outsider->apprentice->warrior->senior_warrior->deputy->leader), quests (3 seeded: 'first-pawsteps','territory-bounds','first-hunt' with objectives/rewards, gameStore.ts:427-536), activeQuests/completedQuests, storySkills{combat,hunting,herbalism,leadership,mysticism,exploration}, clanRelationships, territoryAccess, mysticalConnections, dialog{isOpen,npcName,npcRole,message,options}. Actions: addQuest/updateQuest/completeQuest (awards skill XP + rank)/activateQuest/updateQuestObjective (auto-complete)/addStoryXP/showDialog/closeDialog/toggleQuestBook. Mounted UI: NPCSystem, Dialog, QuestBook, QuestObjectiveOverlay, QuestTracker, Compass (App.tsx:51-67).  · native game/systems/story_mode.hpp
- ✅ **Boot / initial state seeding** [P3] — Native initialize() builds the world, then createPlayer() spawns the cat on the terrain height at origin (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2504-2536) and startWaves() kicks the loop on first Playing entry (2163-2165). Equivalent seeding; the web's global-store handle and its 120/40-minute day-cycle numbers are web-specific plumbing (native day/night is 600s, tracked in the environment domain).
  - web src/components/ui/GameProvider.tsx:19-37: GameProvider seeds initial world + player (initialState.ts: cat 'Shadowpaw', initialPlayerPosition {x:0,y:2,z:0}, world zones/day-night) into the store on mount and exposes the store globally (__GAME_STORE__) for the weapon-XP system (GameProvider.tsx:22-34). Initial day cycle currentTime 0.5 (noon), dayCycleMinutes 120, nightCycleMinutes 40 (gameStore.ts:268-273).  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2504-2536
- 🟡 **Continue-from-save entry point** [P3] — Native exposes an explicit Continue button (MainMenu.setContinueCallback -> continueGame) that scans up to 10 slots for the most-recent save and loadGame()s it (CatAnnihilation.cpp:2288-2312), with setHasSaveGame gating the button. Different resume model (explicit slot-based continue vs implicit autorestore), and native Continue is inert in practice because saveGame is never invoked (no saves ever exist to continue from).
  - web src/lib/store/gameStatePersistence.ts:79-86: Web has no explicit 'Continue' button; instead the store auto-restores gameMode + player/story progress on load (loadGameMode, loadPlayerProgress, loadStoryProgress) so a returning player resumes their persisted progression implicitly. The mode-selection screen still re-appears for the mode/customization pick.  · native game/CatAnnihilation.cpp:2288-2312

> notes: Scope: gameflow-states (menu->playing->paused->gameover, restart, death, story mode P3, save, customization/selection flow). Read in full: web src/lib/store/gameStore.ts, src/App.tsx, contexts/CatCustomizationContext.tsx, gameStatePersistence.ts, GameModeSelection.tsx, GameOverScreen.tsx, PauseMenu.tsx, GameProvider.tsx; native game/CatAnnihilation.hpp + full state-machine section of CatAnnihilation.cpp (355-435, 940-1428, 2038-2536), game/ui/MainMenu.hpp, game/ui/GameUI.hpp, game/systems/cat_customization.hpp, STORY_MODE_DESIGN.md.

Cross-cutting findings: (1) Two native subsystems in this domain are fully built but UNWIRED at runtime -- CatCustomizationSystem (updateCatMaterial/getFurShaderParams never called; no selection UI) and SaveSystem (CatAnnihilation::saveGame() has zero call sites; no autosave; Continue therefore has nothing to load). Marked 'partial' because the code exists but contributes nothing live. (2) Biggest priority-scope (survival) flow divergence is the terminal state: web survival is ENDLESS (only death ends it, no Victory concept), native survival transitions to Victory after finishing wave 5 (CatAnnihilation.cpp:430-432) -- P1. (3) Native uses THREE overlapping state enums (CatAnnihilation GameState, CatAnnihilation GameMode, GameUI GameState with an extra WaveComplete); web has no enum, only Zustand booleans. (4) Web opens on a mode-select + cat-customization + (story) clan-select funnel; native opens on a plain Start/Continue/Settings/Quit menu that jumps straight into arcade survival. (5) Nine-Lives revive is a web death-path interception (revive at 30% maxHealth once per wave, gameStore.ts:677-687) with no native death-flow equivalent even though the ability unlock exists in LevelingSystem. Constants captured verbatim where load-bearing (customization default colors/palettes, revive fraction 0.3, wave-5 victory threshold, day-cycle 120/40 min, survivalHighScore max-tracking). Wave-count scaling and day/night duration numbers deliberately deferred to the waves and environment domains; entries here cover only the flow-state aspects.


## Completeness critic

I now have full coverage of both codebases. Here is the structured enumeration.

# WEB_FILES (React Three Fiber / Three.js / Zustand — the REFERENCE)

**src/ (root)**
- `src/index.tsx` — React DOM entry; mounts `<App/>` in StrictMode, imports global CSS.
- `src/App.tsx` — Root component; wraps `CatCustomizationProvider`>`GameProvider`, always renders `GameModeSelection`, and after a mode is picked lazy-loads all UI + `BasicScene`. Story-only UI (Compass) gated on `storyMode.isActive`.

**src/lib/**
- `src/lib/store/gameStore.ts` — The Zustand store (single source of UI/static state): player, health, inventory, catStats+abilities, weaponSkills, waves, storyMode, quests, day cycle; all setters/actions; RuneScape-style XP formulas. NOT used for dynamic entities.
- `src/lib/store/gameStatePersistence.ts` — localStorage save/load of gameMode, story progress, player progress (cat level/xp, weapon skills, survival high score); keys `cat-annihilation-*`.
- `src/lib/game/initialState.ts` — Static initial player position/cat data (name "Shadowpaw") + world data (zones, heightmap ref, day/night minutes). Mostly legacy/demo seed.

**src/config/**
- `src/config/gameConfig.ts` — `GAME_CONFIG` central constants for the web game (PLAYER speed 6/run 12, ENEMY speed 1.5/dmg 15/range 1.2/cooldown 1000ms/HP 100+20/wave, WEAPONS sword 40+10/lvl, bow 25, magic 20, WAVES base 3 +2/wave ×1.5, cat abilities at lvl 5/10/15/20/25) + enums + XP formulas. NOTE: several systems hardcode these numbers locally instead of importing.
- `src/config/clanCustomizations.ts` — Per-clan base cat appearance + named NPC customizations + random/starter cat generators (story-mode).

**src/contexts/**
- `src/contexts/CatCustomizationContext.tsx` — React context holding player + per-NPC `CatCustomization` (appearance) across the tree.

**src/components/game/**
- `src/components/game/BasicScene.tsx` — Scene router: picks `SurvivalScene` vs `StoryScene` by gameMode/storyModeActive, each wrapped in an auto-retry error boundary. SurvivalScene = R3F `<Canvas>` with sky/fog, `CameraFollow`, lights, `CatCharacter`, `ForestEnvironment`, `GlobalCollisionSystem`, `LocalEnemySystem`, `LocalProjectileSystem`. Also has a legacy inline `Player`/`Tree` (dead-ish).
- `src/components/game/LocalEnemySystem.tsx` — SURVIVAL enemy system (local React state only, never Zustand set). Spawns one generic brown box-dog type in a ring; count = `floor((3+wave*2)*1.5)`, HP `100+(wave-1)*20`, speed 1.5, dmg 15, range 1.2, cooldown 1000ms, separation; sword/shield melee detection, shield-barrier collision, wave progression + transitions. **No dog variants.**
- `src/components/game/LocalProjectileSystem.tsx` — SURVIVAL/story projectiles (local state only); spawns/moves bow arrows + element spells, feeds `globalCollisionData`.
- `src/components/game/GlobalCollisionSystem.tsx` — Shared mutable arrays (`globalCollisionData.projectiles/enemies`, `globalWeaponXP`) + a `useFrame` projectile↔enemy collision loop bridging the local systems; wrapped in collision error boundary.
- `src/components/game/WaveState.ts` — Non-Zustand global wave-transition state + pub/sub (`updateWaveState`, `subscribeToWaveState`); explicitly avoids the store to prevent terrain-clip bug.
- `src/components/game/ForestEnvironment.tsx` — Survival ground plane + procedural grass texture (canvas), trees (cylinder trunk + sphere foliage), fog; robust auto-retry error boundary.
- `src/components/game/NPCSystem.tsx` — STORY-mode NPC spawning/behavior (clan cats via CustomizableCatMesh), terrain/bridge height snap, interaction recording. (story-mode)
- `src/components/game/StoryEncounterSystem.tsx` — STORY practice targets / story-specific enemies feeding collision data. (story-mode)
- `src/components/game/NPCInteractionTracker.ts` — Global NPC-interaction event bus so NPCs notify the quest system without Zustand. (story-mode)
- `src/components/game/UniversalErrorBoundary.tsx` — Reusable configurable error boundary (fallback type + auto-retry).
- `src/components/game/biomes/types.ts` — TS types for biomes/terrain features (BiomeType, BiomeConfig). (story-mode)
- `src/components/game/CatCharacter/index.tsx` — PLAYER cat: WASD movement (`MOVEMENT_SPEED` base, run mult), mouse-look/turn, spacebar/left-click attack, shield, mobile joystick input; drives CatMesh/CustomizableCatMesh + Equipment. Reads terrain collision.
- `src/components/game/CatCharacter/CatMesh.tsx` — Primitive-built animated cat mesh (walk/run/jump/attack/defend anim states).
- `src/components/game/CatCharacter/CustomizableCatMesh.tsx` — Customizable cat mesh + `CatCustomization` type (colors, pattern, ears/tail/fur/body, collar, scars); used for player + NPCs.
- `src/components/game/CatCharacter/Equipment.tsx` — Renders equipped weapon/shield/bow on the cat based on active hotbar item.
- `src/components/game/terrain/SimpleTerrainSystem.tsx` — STORY 600×600 vertex-colored terrain with 5 clan biomes + river cutout + bridges. (story-mode)
- `src/components/game/terrain/TerrainCollisionSystem.tsx` — STORY terrain collision: `terrainCollisionData` (bridges/rivers/staticObjects) + per-frame player push (river block, bridge height). (story-mode; note: writes player position via Zustand in useFrame — the pattern the CLAUDE.md warns about)

**src/components/ui/**
- `src/components/ui/GameModeSelection.tsx` — Start screen: choose Survival vs Story, clan select + cat customization preview (R3F canvas), reset-progress.
- `src/components/ui/GameProvider.tsx` — Seeds initial world/player into the store on mount; exposes store globally for weapon XP.
- `src/components/ui/GameInterface.tsx` — Container with TimeDisplay (day/night clock) + zone info + Dialog/Compass (appears legacy/story overlay). (partly story-mode)
- `src/components/ui/WaveDisplay.tsx` — Survival wave counter; subscribes to `WaveState`.
- `src/components/ui/WaveTransition.tsx` — "Wave Complete / Next Wave" staggered animation overlay (rendered outside Canvas).
- `src/components/ui/CatStats.tsx` — HUD: cat level/XP bar, health, active weapon skill; mobile-aware.
- `src/components/ui/WeaponSkills.tsx` — HUD panel for the active weapon/element skill level+XP.
- `src/components/ui/InventoryHotbar.tsx` — 9-slot (5 on mobile) hotbar, number-key select.
- `src/components/ui/InventoryPopup.tsx` — "I" inventory popup: bag↔quickslot drag/drop, consumables.
- `src/components/ui/SpellBook.tsx` — Spell picker (4 elements) → assigns to hotbar slot 0.
- `src/components/ui/GameOverScreen.tsx` — Death screen with stats + restart.
- `src/components/ui/PauseMenu.tsx` — Pause overlay + sensitivity/move-speed sliders (localStorage).
- `src/components/ui/MobileControls.tsx` — Mobile detection + on-screen movement buttons/joystick synthesizing keyboard events.
- `src/components/ui/VirtualJoystick.tsx` — Touch joystick primitive.
- `src/components/ui/MobilePauseButton.tsx` — On-screen pause button (mobile).
- `src/components/ui/Compass.tsx` — STORY compass with biome/quest/npc/landmark markers. (story-mode)
- `src/components/ui/Dialog.tsx` — STORY NPC dialog box (pauses game, Enter to close). (story-mode)
- `src/components/ui/QuestBook.tsx` — STORY quest journal (available/active/completed, ranks/skills). (story-mode)
- `src/components/ui/QuestObjectiveOverlay.tsx` — STORY on-screen active-objective tracker. (story-mode)
- `src/components/ui/QuestTracker.tsx` — STORY background component auto-updating quest objectives from game state. (story-mode)
